item.content:encoded: (Photo by Vaughn Ridley/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images It might be harder to predict the NBA right now than it has been at any point in league history. The last eight years have produced eight different champions, and no team has even made back-to-back NBA Finals appearances over that time. The second-apron is breaking up contenders early, and an added emphasis on pace-and-space is leading more injuries that make it so much harder to sustain success year-over-over. The NBA season rarely plays out how we think it’s going to. The New York Knicks weren’t exactly a popular preseason pick to win it all last year, and absolutely no one saw the San Antonio Spurs morphing from a 44-win team to the Western Conference champions. The Indiana Pacers made a darkhorse NBA Finals run in 2025, the Dallas Mavericks did the same in 2024, and Miami Heat got all the way there as an 8-seed in 2023. You might think we can already fast-forward to a Thunder-Spurs rematch in the Western Conference Finals this year, but there tends to be a lot more chaos in this era of the league than ever before. With the 2026-27 season here, let’s make our picks for the 2027 NBA Finals and every major award. For more NBA preview coverage, check my list of breakout player candidates , preseason standouts , and preseason rookie rankings . The Raptors win the Eastern Conference I think it’s fair to frame the East as the Knicks vs. the field. I respect the Knicks, but I’d still take the field in that equation, just because it’s so hard to put together consecutive Finals runs in this era. I was choosing between the Raptors and Celtics for my East pick, and I’m going with Toronto for a few reasons. You usually need a top-5 player to make a Finals run, and Kawhi Leonard looked like that type of player last year. I’m well aware of his constant injury issues late in the season, but hey, Toronto did a good job pacing his body last time he was there in 2019, and I think they can do it again. Scottie Barnes is going to have a monster year as Leonard’s sidekick, and when the two share the floor with sophomore Collin Murray-Boyles , it’s going to be impossible to score on Toronto. Ja’Kobe Walter and Jamal Shead are very good role players for this team, and I think Allen Graves can be a contributor off the bench as a rookie, too. Toronto games won’t be pretty, but Kawhi gives them the halfcourt scoring they lacked a year ago, and the rest of the squad should be ready to win a rock fight every night out. The Spurs win the Western Conference The Spurs won 62 games and were the only team in the league to place in the top-3 of both offensive and defensive efficiency last year. The scary thing is I think they will be even better this year. Obviously, it all starts with Victor Wembanyama, who is in the rare position of already being the best player in the world while still having so much room left to improve. Wemby’s defense is multiple levels above any other player on the planet, and I expect we’ll see a more well-rounded offensive game from him this year. Dylan Harper’s sophomore leap is coming, and he’s going to be one of the best guards in the Western Conference before you know it. I’m fascinated to see how San Antonio handles the dynamic between Harper and De’Aaron Fox, but Fox should be better than he was in last year’s playoffs on a bum ankle, and his bloated salary is a problem for another day. Even if I’m not the biggest Stephen Castle guy (cut down the turnovers, man!), San Antonio still has some other great role players, led by Julian Champagnie and Devin Vassell. I think Tobias Harris’ scoring can help out in the halfcourt in a pinch, and I liked their draft haul, too. If any team can sustain consecutive title runs in this era, it’s the Spurs. NBA Finals 2027 prediction: Spurs over Raptors in 6 Kawhi vs. the Spurs for a championship would be absolute cinema. Get me an alternate feed with Uncle Dennis’ color commentary! Toronto’s defense will be nasty, but Wemby is a problem without a solution. I have Wemby getting his first chip at 23 years old. NBA MVP 2027 pick: Victor Wembanyama Boring answer, I know. Luka Doncic was my backup choice. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander in 2025 is the only NBA MVP to win the championship in the last decade, so it won’t be easy, but it feels like Wemby is destined to pull off a few of these double-dips in his career. Might as well start now. NBA Defensive Player of the Year: Victor Wembanyama It’s a lock if he plays 65 games. If he doesn’t, I’d go with OKC’s Chet Holmgren, who is fantastic when he plays anyone but Wembanyama . NBA Rookie of the Year 2027 pick: Cameron Boozer, F, Memphis Grizzlies It’s a straight up crime that Boozer wasn’t the No. 1 overall pick, because he was very clearly the best prospect in the draft . Boozer is literally the youngest player in the NBA this season with a July 2007 birthday, but I fully expect him to be Memphis’ best player from the jump. Pick a play type, any play type, and Boozer is already excellent at it. He can body people in the pick-and-roll as the handler or screener, he can nail three-pointers off the dribble or the catch, he can drive, he can clean the offensive glass for putbacks, he can crush the offensive glass like a traditional big man, and he’s an expert decision-maker with the ball in his hands. No rookie has made All-NBA since Tim Duncan in 1998, but I think Boozer can challenge for a spot this year. NBA Coach of the Year prediction: Joe Mazzulla, Boston Celtics The Celtics are my pick to earn the No. 1 seed in the East this year, and if Mazzulla pulls that off after the Jaylen Brown trade , he’s going to get hailed as a genius. Mazzulla optimizes every possession for success in a way no other coach can match. His teams have a clear identity of launching threes, hitting the offensive glass with aggression (hello, Mitchell Robinson), and challenging every shot at the rim. It brings me no joy to predict greatness for the Celtics , but I really think it’s going to happen this season. NBA Sixth Man of the Year pick: Ajay Mitchell, G, Oklahoma City Thunder Mitchell was one of last season’s breakout players, but it felt like he never got the recognition he deserved because injuries limited him to 57 games (taking away award consideration) and put him on the sidelines for OKC’s most important playoff games. The former UC Santa Barbara product can provide everything teams want from a secondary ball handler with airtight driving ability, improved outside shooting, and a knack for finding teammates without turning the ball over. SGA can’t do everything for the Thunder, and Mitchell will be there to pick to the scraps as the Thunder put together another dominant season. NBA Most Improved Player 2027 pick: Scoot Henderson, G, Portland Trail Blazers Henderson looks fantastic in preseason for the Blazers team that is no longer counting on him to be a savior with Damian Lillard and Ja Morant entrenched in the starting backcourt. I think it’s only a matter of time before Scoot breaks up that pairing, because his feisty on-ball defense, improved three-point stroke, and extra gear going to the basket makes him the most well-rounded guard in Portland’s backcourt. He’s slated to be a restricted free agent after this season, and he should have plenty of suitors if he finally starts living up to his former draft hype in his fourth season. NBA Clutch Player of the Year 2027 pick: Jalen Brunson, G, New York Knicks The NBA will be bending over backwards to give him this award if he hits a few clutch shots this year as a make-up call from last season. Brunson is the most terrifying clutch demon in the league, the Knicks are going to be awesome again, and he should win this award going away. All-NBA Team 2027 picks and predictions First-Team: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Thunder Luka Doncic, Lakers Giannis Antetokounmpo, Heat Nikola Jokic, Nuggets Victor Wembanyama, Spurs Second-Team: Jalen Brunson, Knicks Anthony Edwar

item.title: Scaling the Rocks: Game 6? Game 7? Rays? Guardians?
item.description: CLEVELAND, OHIO - OCTOBER 18: Bryan Baker #47 and Junior Caminero #13 of the Tampa Bay Rays celebrate the 3-1 win over the Cleveland Guardians in game five of the American League Championship Series at Progressive Field on October 18, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tampa Bay Rays won Game 5 against the Cleveland Guardians, putting them one win away from potentially winning their first World Series. The Guardians will look to spoil that tonight and force Game 7, which would put them in the World Series for the first time since 2016 and once again within striking distance of their first win since 1948. It was a relatively slow weekend in Rockies land, but here’s what folks had to say about the team as well as others around the league: Rockies News & Links 3 Rockies prospects to watch in 2027 | MLB.com While there are plenty of Major League roster questions, Thomas Harding offers three prospects for fans to keep an eye on in 2027 (especially if there is a lockout) — Mason Adams ( No. 17 PuRP ), Charlie Condon ( No. 2 PuRP ) and Jackson Cox ( No. 11 PuRP ). Rockies part ways with pitching coach Leichman after 1 season | MLB.com We all know that the Rockies fired Alon Leichman after a rookie season that saw a lot of experimentation with the rotation. Nobody quite knows why the Rockies let Leichman go, but Thomas Harding provides more details as to potentially what went wrong between the two parties. Banana Ball returning to Coors Field in May 2027 for two games | Denver7 Banana Ball is returning to Coors Field in 2027, but it won’t feature the Savannah Bananas this time. It will feature the Party Animals and the Loco Beach Coconuts, which feature old friend Will Ethridge . Enter the lottery here if you haven’t already. Have you been to a Banana Ball game yet? Around MLB Jean Fruth and the Importance of Storytelling in Growing Women’s Baseball | SABR A few weeks ago, our own Joelle Milhom presented at the eight annual SABR-IWBC Women in Baseball Conference. You can watch her presentation here! I covered the end of the Yankees’ dynasty. Here’s what happens next for the Dodgers | The Athletic ($) The Dodgers are out of the playoffs! Tyler Kepner makes his predictions for what will happen now that the three-peat (and maybe the lockout??) is out of the picture. He identifies all of the things that he thinks will happen: MLB will try to stop them They will keep winning … except in October Other powers will emerge They will take on other teams’ big contracts (Hey Dodgers, can we interest you in Kris Bryant ??) item.title: Kansas City Royals news: Carter Jensen beats the drum
item.description: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - JULY 17: Carter Jensen, center, is mobbed by his Kansas City Royals teammates after his two-RBI single gave them the win over the San Diego Padres at Kauffman Stadium on July 17, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Reed Hoffmann/Getty Images) | Getty Images Chris Higgins at the Star writes about the biggest unanswered questions from the downtown ballpark presentation. Brooks Sherman, president of real estate and development for the Royals, said on Thursday that master planning for the ballpark district is getting started now as the team looks to hire a master planner. “Right now our focus is on the stadium,” he said. Sherman said there have been no decisions about any demolitions in Crown Center and that there are great tenants already on site whom officials look to keep and add to. Jared Bush at Fox4 has more . “That’s when we begin to look at the entirety of the rest of the district to understand what kind of buildings we would have, an entertainment venue, the retail, the food and beverage and so forth, so there have been no decisions about any destruction on any building.” Sherman said there are a lot of great tenants at Crown Center, and they want to keep all of them. One of those, just north of 25th Street and the Hallmark-owned Kaleidoscope, is the Sea Life Aquarium. That entity told us to reach out to Hallmark about demolition. “The development will reimagine Crown Center and revitalize the city’s original live-work-play neighborhood while strengthening our business community and creating new opportunities,” one of the spokespeople for Hallmark said. “We remain in the early phases of planning the district beyond the ballpark. We are committed to maintaining open communication with our tenants and business partners as plans progress.” Philip Ruo at Royals Keep has thoughts on Randy Dobnak. Dobnak excelled in limiting hitters to a 3.7% barrel rate and inducing ground balls at a 51.2% rate. While this is a good recipe for limiting home runs and extra-base hits, Dobnak struggled with striking out batters, and batters were too easily able to make contact off him. One of Dobnak’s biggest weaknesses was his inability to miss bats. Hitters made contact on 91% of their swings at pitches in the strike zone (league worst), leaving him heavily reliant on his defense to record outs. His 4.22 FIP, more than a run higher than his ERA, suggests his results could be difficult to sustain. David Laurila at Fangraphs talks to Tyler Tolbert about his improving bat. “I’m just continuing to get better,” said Tolbert, whose .246 batting average and .693 OPS while coming up through the Royals system didn’t exactly portend his recent level of success. “Each season you just try to find what works for you, and try to get into a groove. I’ve had good hitting years and I’ve had average hitting years. I don’t really chase numbers, though. I just trust my routine and my process. item.title: 4 biggest risers in College Football after Week 7
item.description: What a wild week of college football . Because 5 of the AP top-10 teams lost this week, there has to be a new batch of teams ready to take their place, and we had some teams rise to the occasion here in Week 7. Here are the biggest risers of the week. MORE: Biggest 24-team College Football Playoff issue no one is talking about BYU Oct 9, 2026; Provo, Utah, USA; BYU Cougars quarterback Bear Bachmeier (47) warms up prior to a game against the Iowa State Cyclones at LaVell Edwards Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Aaron Baker-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) It may have been a controversial ending, but the Cougars notched one of their biggest wins in program history, knocking off Notre Dame 28-24. This is massive for a BYU team hoping to avoid a repeat of 2024 and 2025, when two-loss Cougar teams were left out of the CFP for not having enough marquee wins. Now, thanks to the incredible efforts of Bear Bachmeier and co., they have a massive marquee win in 2026. UCLA Sep 5, 2026; Berkeley, California, USA; UCLA Bruins head coach Bob Chesney (center) talks to UCLA Bruins linebacker Jalen Woods (left) before the game against the California Golden Bears at California Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images Even without QB1 Nico Iamaleava, the Bruins outlasted Wisconsin and came away with a 17-7 win. It certainly wasn’t pretty, but it was significant. Looking at the rest of UCLA’s schedule, they don’t have to play Ohio State or Indiana. Their toughest remaining game is the Battle for LA against USC. 12-0 is within sight for the Bruins, which would obviously guarantee a CFP berth in Bob Chesney’s first season. Ole Miss Sep 26, 2026; Gainesville, Florida, USA; Mississippi Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss (6) looks to throw against the Florida Gators during the second half at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images In a week when the rest of the AP top-10 was losing, Ole Miss put a beatdown on Missouri. Trinidad Chambliss accounted for 4 total touchdowns in the 31-3 rout. The longer we move away from it, the more that Ole Miss’s loss to Florida looks like a one-time aberration. The Rebels look like an SEC contender and have one of the country’s best quarterbacks leading the way. Tennessee Oct 17, 2026; Knoxville, Tennessee, USA; Tennessee Volunteers running back DeSean Bishop (18) celebrates with teammates after scoring a touchdown against the Alabama Crimson Tide during the second half at Neyland Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Randy Sartin-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) All of a sudden, Tennessee looks like an SEC contender as well. The Volunteers were never really threatened in a 26-10 victory over rival Alabama. It was George MacIntyre, not freshman Faizon Brandon, who started at QB for the Vols, and while his numbers were unspectacular, he played complementary football to an elite run game and defensive effort and got the job done. Desean B

item.title: Lions vs. Packers odds: Opening lines for Week 7 matchup
item.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 27: Jameson Williams #1 of the Detroit Lions scores a touchdown during the second quarter against the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field on November 27, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions (3-2) will host their division rival Green Bay Packers (4-2) in Week 7, and the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -3.5 points . The Packers finished their 2025 season by snagging the seven seed in the playoffs, but the Bears eliminated them in the Wild Card round. Packers defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley was hired to be the next head coach of the Miami Dolphins, and Green Bay hired Jonathan Gannon (previously the head coach of the Cardinals) as a replacement. With Gannon came a new 3-4 defense and a whole bunch of changes on the defensive side of the ball. EDGE Rashan Gary was traded to the Cowboys, NT Colby Wooden was traded to the Colts, while EDGE Kingsley Enagbare, MIKE Quay Walker, and CB Nate Hobbs departed in free agency. EDGE/LB Micah Parsons continues to recover from an ACL tear and is not expected to be available in Week 7. Being up against the cap, the Packers elected to promote from within, inserting EDGE Lukas Van Ness and ILB Isaiah McDuffie into the starting lineup, trading for LB Zaire Franklin (who is starting in place of injured Edgerrin Cooper), and drafting starters CB Brandon Cisse (second round) and NT Chris McClellan (third) on Day 2 of the NFL Draft. On offense, the Packers lost QB Malik Willis, RB Emanuel Wilson, WR Dontayvion Wicks (traded to the Eagles), WR Romeo Dobbs, LT Rasheed Walker, and LG/C Elgton Jenkins; like on defense, they elected to mostly promote from within, elevating RB Marshawn Lloyd into a bigger role (especially with Josh Jacobs suspended—he is expected to return in Week 7), WR Savion Williams and LT Jordan Morgan into the starting lineup, and shifting Sean Rhyan inside to center. Their guard spots have been a massive problem, and the Packers have been searching for answers, with their most recent pairing being RG Travis Glover and former Lion LG Laken Tomlinson (starting in place of the injured Aaron Banks). After a slow start to their 2026 season, the Packers have settled down as their offense has found its groove. The Packers opened the season with a loss after allowing the Vikings to drop 39 points on them, rebounded in Week 2 by beating the Jets by three points, only to lose again in Week 3 as the Falcons dominated them on the ground to the tune of 35 points. In Week 4, the Packers once again found a way to win by three points, this time over the Bucs, then smashed a Caleb Williams-less Bears team 31-7. In Week 6, the Packers took on the Cowboys’ 31st-ranked defense on “Sunday Night Football,” and while they jumped out to a 17-0 lead in the first half, they only scored six points in the second half. Fortunately, their defense held strong and allowed only 13 points, and the game end

item.title: Syracuse men’s basketball: Orange face injury woes following Siena win
item.description: Garwey Dual takes a jumper against Siena | Tom Windhausen-CuseNation Sports Gerry McNamara shared some less than ideal news in his post-game press conference following the 81-76 win over Siena , with multiple players dealing with injuries. Syracuse basketball injury update: •Kiyan Anthony and Tassie Goodrick are dealing with knee tendinitis •Garwey Dual is working through a sprained ankle • Aiden Tobiason has a hamstring issue “I’d imagine it’s going to be a few weeks.” pic.twitter.com/m9PfrXeK6Q — James Szuba (@JamesSzuba) October 18, 2026 Kiyan Anthony and Tasman Goodrick both have knee tendinitis, which kept Goodrick out of the Sunday exhibition. Anthony managed to play against the Saints, but only for 8 minutes where he tallied one rebound and two fouls, and after sitting for a little while McNamara found it best to sit him for the remainder of the contest. Syracuse did get Mark Morano back, who went for 18 points in his first game with the Orange on 4-6 outside shooting. Morano confirmed to TNIAAM that he was dealing with a hamstring strain but feels “great” now. Garwey Dual has another injury after dealing with a dislocated collarbone earlier in the summer, he now has a sprained ankle which happened during the UConn game last week. Dual played only 12 minutes against Siena, but was productive with 8 points and 5 rebounds. He’s been back to practice just a couple weeks at full speed following the collarbone injury. “I’m probably two weeks back now,” Dual said post-game. “I’m obviously still trying to get back to where I was before the surgery. I’m just trying to be better.” Lastly, and most importantly, Temple transfer Aiden Tobiason will be out a few weeks after he injured his hamstring within the first minute of the game against UConn. The exact specifics of the injury are not clear, but it certainly isn’t good for the Orange with their season kicking off in two weeks time.

item.title: Best Week 7 fantasy football waiver wire pickups at QB, RB, WR, TE
item.description: CLEVELAND, OHIO - OCTOBER 1: Germie Bernard #17 of the Pittsburgh Steelers stands for the national anthem prior to a game against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on October 1, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to the Week 7 waiver wire brought to you by injuries and breakout games. Injuries have been the one constant this season, and they’ve had most of us scrambling to the wire to put in our claims for some painful and not so painful backups, especially at running back. If you picked up Najee Harris or Jaleel McLaughlin for spot starts in Week 6, you were not happy with your decision. But, if you grabbed Dameon Pierce or Roschon Johnson for that start, you likely are feeling good that both got into the end zone. That’s usually the way things go with backup backs, as a touchdown can make or break their fantasy day since they aren’t putting up bell cow back numbers in relief. This week we have a few strong pickups, but mostly at the receiver position, as some young guys stepped up big this week. We’ll use Yahoo’s rostership percentages and try to stick under 50% if possible. Week 7 byes We have some strong players on bye, as the Buffalo Bills, Jacksonville Jaguars. Los Angeles Chargers, and Washington Commanders will take a week off. Quarterbacks Kyler Murray, Vikings (51%) Murray was on bye this week, but the previous week was his best fantasy game of the early season. Getting Justin Jefferson back and healthy was huge for Murray. Plus, in their win over the Saints, he rushed 10 times for 51 yards. That is great to see for his fantasy upside. This week they face a Colts team at home that has allowed the 7th-most fantasy points and rushing yards to opposing quarterbacks. He also should get TE T.J. Hockenson back from a concussion. Plus, Murray faces the Lions and Bills after the Colts. Both teams have been giving up big fantasy points to quarterbacks, but will also push their opponents due to their strong offenses. Geno Smith, Jets (7%) Smith has been up and down with the Jets so far, but he has shown enough to believe there is upside in good matchups. And this week he gets a great matchup against a Dolphins team that is very much in tank mode. Add in the breakout by rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. today, and you have a great new weapon for Smith. With Garrett Wilson already manning the No. 1 slot and Adonai Mitchell possibly returning next week, Smith should be poised for a good game. Running backs Kendre Miller, Saints (34%) Miller didn’t have a big fantasy day against the Giants on Sunday, but he did get 22 touches in their win. He finished with 70 total yards and didn’t find pay dirt, but the usage was great. He’ll face a good Steelers defense in Paris next week, but one that has been middling against the run. The Saints then have a bye in Week 8. It’s tough to find usage like his on waivers, but we also don’t want to go all in on a guy who hasn’t shown much upside. Ba

(Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to the Week 7 waiver wire brought to you by injuries and breakout games. Injuries have been the one constant this season, and they’ve had most of us scrambling to the wire to put in our claims for some painful and not so painful backups, especially at running back. If you picked up Najee Harris or Jaleel McLaughlin for spot starts in Week 6, you were not happy with your decision. But, if you grabbed Dameon Pierce or Roschon Johnson for that start, you likely are feeling good that both got into the end zone. That’s usually the way things go with backup backs, as a touchdown can make or break their fantasy day since they aren’t putting up bell cow back numbers in relief. This week we have a few strong pickups, but mostly at the receiver position, as some young guys stepped up big this week. We’ll use Yahoo’s rostership percentages and try to stick under 50% if possible. Week 7 byes We have some strong players on bye, as the Buffalo Bills, Jacksonville Jaguars. Los Angeles Chargers, and Washington Commanders will take a week off. Quarterbacks Kyler Murray, Vikings (51%) Murray was on bye this week, but the previous week was his best fantasy game of the early season. Getting Justin Jefferson back and healthy was huge for Murray. Plus, in their win over the Saints, he rushed 10 times for 51 yards. That is great to see for his fantasy upside. This week they face a Colts team at home that has allowed the 7th-most fantasy points and rushing yards to opposing quarterbacks. He also should get TE T.J. Hockenson back from a concussion. Plus, Murray faces the Lions and Bills after the Colts. Both teams have been giving up big fantasy points to quarterbacks, but will also push their opponents due to their strong offenses. Geno Smith, Jets (7%) Smith has been up and down with the Jets so far, but he has shown enough to believe there is upside in good matchups. And this week he gets a great matchup against a Dolphins team that is very much in tank mode. Add in the breakout by rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. today, and you have a great new weapon for Smith. With Garrett Wilson already manning the No. 1 slot and Adonai Mitchell possibly returning next week, Smith should be poised for a good game. Running backs Kendre Miller, Saints (34%) Miller didn’t have a big fantasy day against the Giants on Sunday, but he did get 22 touches in their win. He finished with 70 total yards and didn’t find pay dirt, but the usage was great. He’ll face a good Steelers defense in Paris next week, but one that has been middling against the run. The Saints then have a bye in Week 8. It’s tough to find usage like his on waivers, but we also don’t want to go all in on a guy who hasn’t shown much upside. Bam Knight, Cardinals (0%) Knight outplayed Tyler Allgeier in their win against the Rams on Sunday, rushing 15 times for 80 yards and catching two passes for 18 more yards. Allgeier on the other hand rushed 18 times for just 38 yards and caught one pass for 10 more. There was little doubt that Knight had more juice than Allgeier and if Jeremiyah Love can’t get back for their home game against the Broncos, I’d expect Knight to get plenty of chances to pick up where he left off. But, if Love is back, Knight loses waiver wire appeal. Samaje Perine, Bengals (5%) Perine out-played Chase Brown in their win over the Dolphins in Week 5 and should have won more work moving forward. He’s not a must-add, but the Bengals’ offense is good enough to help Perine put up usable fantasy numbers if he continues to see a big chunk of the work. Other RBs worth a look — Tyrone Tracy, Corey Kiner, Jordan Mason Wide receivers Germie Bernard, Steelers (50%) Bernard has seen increased usage with Michael Pittman and Roman Wilson out, but this week was his breakout. The rookie caught 11 passes for 87 yards and the game winning touchdown in overtime against the Buccaneers. Bernard is good on underneath routes and that fits Aaron Rodgers, who is a check down merchant at this point in his career. This matchup with the blitz happy Bucs fit Bernard’s underneath work well, as Rodgers needed to get rid of the ball quickly. That might not always be the case, but Rodgers has shown an affinity for quick hitters and Bernard fits the bill. Omar Cooper Jr., Jets (4%) The rookie caught six passes for 103 yards and a touchdown against the Patriots. This was his first game back from his ankle injury, which is fairly miraculous. Adonai Mitchell missed his fourth game with his finger injury, which helped Cooper see more snaps in his first game back. But, Cooper is a first round pick who just put up great numbers in his first full game in the NFL. The Jets have no reason to not make him a big part of their offense moving forward. Jaylin Noel, Texans (7%) Noel had a huge game against the Jaguars across the pond Sunday morning, as he caught four passes for 107 yards and a touchdown. There’s talent there to be sure and he’s worth rostering if you can fit him, but the Texans and C.J. Stroud are going to spread the ball around. And, with Marvin Harrison Jr. added to the rotation, it’s still going to be difficult to pick the right Texans’ fantasy wide receiver not name Nico Collins. Other WRs worth a look — Travis Hunter, Darius Cooper, Kendrick Bourne, Demario Douglas, Ja’Kobi Lane Tight end T.J. Hockenson, Vikings (31%) Hockenson suffered a concussion early in Week 5, but should be ready to return following their Week 6 bye. He hasn’t had a great season so far, but his 13 receptions for 119 yards in Week 4 against the Dolphins shows us that Kyler Murray has no reservations in throwing to his tight end. Also, he gets a strong matchup against the Colts in Week 7, who have given up big games to Travis Kelce and Pat Freiermuth so far this season. Other TEs worth a look —Brenton Strange, Hunter Henry, Mike Gesicki D/STs Jets (7%) vs. Dolphins The Jets face the Dolphins at home. Miami hasn’t allowed any D/ST to score under 8 fantasy points this season and despite coming off their bye, there’s no reason to believe they are close to competing this season. Browns (20%) at Titans (2%) Both of these teams are in the Top 7 in giving up fantasy points to D/STs. It might not be pretty, but if I need a D/ST off waivers this week, I have no qualms with taking either of these teams.

item.title: Arizona football enters tough 2nd half with Big 12 title game, playoff bid still in play
item.description: TUCSON, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 19: Arizona Wildcats hold block A flag to start the third quarter against the Northern Illinois Huskies at Casino Del Sol Stadium on September 19, 2026 in Tucson, Arizona. (Photo by Patrick Mulligan/Getty Images) | Getty Images The last time Arizona started a season 5-1, in 2014, it matched that record in the second half and made its lone appearance in a conference title game. Replicating its first half this time could result in a spot in the College Football Playoff. Back in the AP Top 25 despite being on a bye, the Wildcats get back to work this week with a Homecoming matchup against Iowa State. That’s one of four games set for Casino Del Sol Stadium, including the Territorial Cup in November. A win on Saturday will secure bowl eligibility for the UA for the second consecutive season, which last happened in 2014-15. But just getting to play a 13 th game is not the only goal within reach, as it is very much in the hunt for a spot in the Big 12 championship. At 2-1 in Big 12 play, Arizona is tied with Baylor and Oklahoma State for 5 th place. There are three teams in the league (BYU, Texas Tech and Utah) without a loss and the top two will play in Arlington on Dec. 4 with at least one CFP spot on the line. The Wildcats have already played BYU, falling 28-17 in Provo for their only loss, while Tech and Utah are still to come. The Red Raiders host Arizona on Oct. 31, and two weeks later Utah comes to Tucson. There are also matchups with TCU (Nov. 6) and at Kansas State (Nov. 21) along with the T-Cup against ASU on Nov. 28. Arizona’s six remaining opponents have a combined record of 25-11, with everyone at .500 or better. That’s compared to the first six foes, who are a combined 21-19, and six of those wins come from FCS Northern Arizona. A year ago, the Wildcats were 4-2 at the halfway point and, after a walkoff loss at Houston, won the next five and climbed to 17 th in the final playoff rankings. Their best CFP ranking came in 2014, when they sat at No. 7 heading into the Pac-12 Championship Game back when the playoff only included four teams.

item.title: MLB Playoff Roundup: Rays smother Guardians, move within one win of AL pennant
item.description: Oct 18, 2026; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Tampa Bay Rays outfielder Victor Mesa Jr. (25)and Tampa Bay Rays second baseman Richie Palacios (1) react after game five of the ALCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Progressive Field. Mandatory Credit: David Dermer-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect When the Guardians went up two games to one in this American League Championship Series, their goal was pretty simple. Even a split of their final two games in Cleveland would keep them in control, headed back to Tampa Bay with two shots to end the ALCS and return to the World Series for the first time since 2016. Instead, the Rays did what the Rays do. They made things hard on their opponent, they pitched the lights out, and they won two games in a row, including a smothering performance in Game 5 last night. Indeed, it will be the Rays that head back to Florida with two chances to win the pennant. American League Championship Series Game 5 Tampa Bay Rays 3, Cleveland Guardians 1 (Rays lead series 3-2) The score line reads this as a close ballgame, and nominally, it was, with the Rays never able to put away the Guardians, and Cleveland ultimately bringing the tying run to the plate in each of the final two innings. As it was played, though, it never really felt close. Tampa Bay’s offense kept traffic on the base paths all night, while Cleveland could nary string a rally together, leading to a 3-1 Rays win that wasn’t as tight as the score indicated. In the early innings, it felt as though Tampa really would run away with it. They were all over Guardians lefty Parker Messick, who had a fantastic 2026 season but has looked as though he might be buckling under a career-high workload. Messick struggled with his control, and after the Rays loaded the bases in the first on a Yandy Díaz double, a walk to Ryan Vilade, and a Chandler Simpson single, Messick forced in the game’s first run by walking Jonny DeLuca. Messick avoided further damage by stranding the bases loaded with a Liam Hicks groundout, but he went right back in the spin cycle the next inning. Singles from Ben Williamson, Díaz, and Jonathan Aranda doubled Tampa Bay’s lead to 2-0, and Messick needed key strikeouts of Vilade and Junior Caminero just to hold the line there. View Link Though the Rays led by just two after two, the way things were playing out left manager Stephen Vogt in an unenviable position. His top young lefty was getting slowcooked by the Rays’ offense, having thrown 57 pitches to get six outs, but Vogt had come into the game wanting much more from Messick, with this series possibly set to have four games played on consecutive nights, and the Guardians likely to deploy a bullpen game in Game 6 tonight. item.content:encoded: Oct 18, 2026; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Tampa Bay Rays outfielder Victor Mesa Jr. (25)and Tampa Bay Rays second baseman Richie Palacios (1) react after game five of the ALCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Progressive Field. Mandatory Credit: David Dermer-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect When the Guardians went up two games to one in this American League Championship Series, their goal was pretty simple. Even a split of their final two games in Cleveland would keep them in control, headed back to Tampa Bay with two shots to end the ALCS and return to the World Series for the first time since 2016. Instead, the Rays did what the Rays do. They made things hard on their opponent, they pitched the lights out, and they won two games in a row, including a smothering performance in Game 5 last night. Indeed, it will be the Rays that head back to Florida with two chances to win the pennant. American League Championship Series Game 5 Tampa Bay Rays 3, Cleveland Guardians 1 (Rays lead series 3-2) The score line reads this as a close ballgame, and nominally, it was, with the Rays never able to put away the Guardians, and Cleveland ultimately bringing the tying run to the plate in each of the final two innings. As it was played, though, it never really felt close. Tampa Bay’s offense kept traffic on the base paths all night, while Cleveland could nary string a rally together, leading to a 3-1 Rays win that wasn’t as tight as the score indicated. In the early innings, it felt as though Tampa really would run away with it. They were all over Guardians lefty Parker Messick, who had a fantastic 2026 season but has looked as though he might be buckling under a career-high workload. Messick struggled with his control, and after the Rays loaded the bases in the first on a Yandy Díaz double, a walk to Ryan Vilade, and a Chandler Simpson single, Messick forced in the game’s first run by walking Jonny DeLuca. Messick avoided further damage by stranding the bases loaded with a Liam Hicks groundout, but he went right back in the spin cycle the next inning. Singles from Ben Williamson, Díaz, and Jonathan Aranda doubled Tampa Bay’s lead to 2-0, and Messick needed key strikeouts of Vilade and Junior Caminero just to hold the line there. View Link Though the Rays led by just two after two, the way things were playing out left manager Stephen Vogt in an unenviable position. His top young lefty was getting slowcooked by the Rays’ offense, having thrown 57 pitches to get six outs, but Vogt had come into the game wanting much more from Messick, with this series possibly set to have four games played on consecutive nights, and the Guardians likely to deploy a bullpen game in Game 6 tonight. It spoke to the gravity of the situation that even with all that, Vogt pulled Messick, and tabbed Tim Herrin to start the third. Herrin fared no better. Simpson doubled to lead off and stole third, before coming home on Hicks’ RBI single: View Link Herrin induced a double play from Williamson to end the inning there, the first of two Cleveland double plays that were key in keeping the Rays from blowing things open. Tampa had grinded out eight hits and two walks in the first two innings, and Cleveland had to feel fortunate to only be down three, but their task remained tall, in no small part thanks to a man that’s authoring quite the postseason legend this October. Drew Rasmussen started for Tampa and was his usual excellent self. He shut out the Guardians through the first five innings, and didn’t allow a runner as far as second base until the sixth. There, Steven Kwan and José Ramírez stacked back-to-back singles, and Chase DeLauter drove home Kwan with an RBI groundout to finally damage Rasmussen. But that was the only trouble Rasmussen found himself in. Nathaniel Lowe led off the seventh with a single, but Rasmussen got Travis Bazanna to foul out before Patrick Bailey grounded into a double play to end the inning. That would be it for Rasmussen, who exited having allowed one run on four hits over seven, striking out six. Kevin Cash went with Cam Booser in the eighth, who retired the first two batters before allowing a single to Kwan. On came Tyler Wells to face Ramírez as the tying run, blowing a high cut-fastball past Ramírez in a 2-2 count to end the inning: View Link That left the ninth for Rays closer Bryan Baker, who briefly looked like he might inject a bit of drama into the proceedings by walking DeLauter to open the frame. But on the first pitch he saw from Baker, Jo Adell grounded a tailor-made double play ball to Taylor Walls, who got the out at short but saw Richie Palacios spike the throw to first to give Adell a reprieve. No matter, Baker got Lowe to foul out and Bazzana to ground out to cinch a 14-pitch save. The Rays never did blow this one open, which is notable because of what that feat cost Cleveland: Vogt ended up going deep into his bullpen. All of Vogt’s high-leverage arms, Cade Smith, Hunter Gaddis, and Erik Sabrowski, ended up getting more than three outs last night, while Herrin and Shawn Armstrong also contributed to the effort. None of them threw more than 22 pitches (Smith), but they all ended up taxing themselves in a loss before having to get on a plane to go to Tampa with the prospect of two more bullpen-heavy games looming. Not only do the Guardians need to win two on the road, but their bullpen will be behind the eight-ball as they try to do so. This series is certainly not over; we need only go back to Game 3 to find an instance of Cleveland doing enough to win without needing to ask much from their pitching staff. But the Guardians have exhausted their margin of error. They now need to be close to perfect on back-to-back nights, while the Rays need just one more strong effort to clinch the pennant. They’ll have their first shot at it tonight at 8 p.m. EST when they send Freddy Peralta to the mound.

item.title: Nate George and Enddy Azocar: Two outfielders, two different paths
item.description: PORT CHARLOTTE, FL - MARCH 18: Nate George (11) of the Baltimore Orioles runs in from the field during a minor league spring training game against the Tampa Bay Rays on March 18, 2026 at Charlotte Sports Park in Port Charlotte, Florida. (Photo by Joe Robbins/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images On the surface, it might feel like Nate George and Enddy Azocar are an unlikely pairing for our prospect review series. And it’s true, their 2026 seasons had very different trajectories. But they are both talented outfielders who weren’t heralded signings when they joined pro ball in 2024. They are both above-average defenders, which is always exciting after watching the Orioles’ current defense. And they both played for the High-A Frederick Keys, though not at the same time. These two had almost opposite arcs over the course of the season. George’s year was highly anticipated after he shot up the prospect lists with his 2025 performance. Azocar, however, struggled in 2025 and was looking to get into the top prospect discussion (spoiler: he did). Now the two sit back-to-back on the Orioles prospect list at MLB Pipeline ; Azocar is #6 and George is #7. Nate George At the end of 2025, Nate George was a star on the rise. The Orioles drafted him in the 16th round of the 2024 draft. By the end of the next season, everyone was taking notice. He was awarded the team’s Minor League Prospect of the Year in 2025, was named a top 100 prospect by Baseball America, and was at the top of Orioles’ prospect lists. He did so by spending his 19th year laying waste to the Florida Coast League and Low-A, then finishing off the season with a .380 OBP in 21 games with the high-A Aberdeen IronBirds. His full 2025 numbers: .336/.413/.483 with 50 stolen bases. He is also an above-average fielder with a ton of speed, making him perhaps even more enticing than Enrique Bradfield, Jr., who has the defense but struggles offensively. When the 2026 minor league rosters were announced, the High-A Frederick Keys had an enviable lineup. George joined fellow prospects Ike Irish and Wehiwa Aloy to make a formidable threesome. But it didn’t last long. George was off to a pretty good start when, after 20 games, he was put on the injured list with a non-baseball-related medical condition. George was hitting .293/.372/.366 with 15 SB when he left the team. He did not play for the rest of the year. There have been no real updates on George since he was removed from the active roster at the beginning of May. It hurts for a prospect to lose so much development time, but more than that, I think we can agree that we just hope he’s doing ok as a person. I expect we’ll get news of some sort as we approach spring training. Enddy Azocar The same year that Nate George was drafted #489 overall, the Boston Red Sox signed Enddy Azocar out of Venezuela for just $40,000. Azocar made his professional debut that year in the Dominican Summer League, then started strong in 2025 in th

Enddy Azocar The same year that Nate George was drafted #489 overall, the Boston Red Sox signed Enddy Azocar out of Venezuela for just $40,000. Azocar made his professional debut that year in the Dominican Summer League, then started strong in 2025 in the Florida Coast League. After just 14 games, the Red Sox promoted him to low-A Salem. Unlike George, Azocar struggled in low-A. Over 71 games he failed to get on base (.273 OBP) and failed to hit for power (.315 SLG). He was young for the league, about 2.5 years younger than the average player. It was a struggle he apparently learned from, because 2026 was much different. Azocar began 2026 with the same team he finished 2025 with, the low-A Salem Red Sox. Same team, but he appeared to be a different player. He started strong at the plate, OPS’ing .868 in May and .907 in April. His power jumped up, too. By the end of May, Azocar had seven home runs. He hit only six in all of 2025. His improved numbers earned him a promotion to high-A, and he stumbled against the higher competition. June was his worst month of the season, but he adjusted. In July, he hit eight home runs and OPS’d 1.046 in 19 games. On August 3rd, Azocar was traded to the Orioles in the package that sent Adley Rutschman to the Red Sox. He debuted with the Frederick Keys the next day and made a very good first impression. Azocar had three hits in his organizational debut and 10 hits over his first five games. He finished out the year with the Keys and hit .327/.372/.529 in 25 games. At just 19, Azocar was still young for the league he played in. But this time around, he thrived. Between the two orgs, he played well at High-A for 71 games. I expect he’ll start 2027 with the Double-A Chesapeake Baysox. Azocar has played multiple outfield positions, but on all three teams in 2026 he spent the majority of his time in center field. Per MLB Pipeline, he has good instincts and average range in center, but is much better suited to a corner outfield position. Luckily for him, the Orioles need defensive help at all positions. George and Azocar are both young, talented outfielders in the Orioles’ system. They had different paths in 2026, but we hope to see them both continue to succeed in 2027.

item.title: Falcons – Bears Week 6 recap: A whole lot of stumbling
item.description: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 18: Bijan Robinson #7 of the Atlanta Falcons rushes during the first quarter against the Chicago Bears at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons turned in two glorious weeks where they beat down the Packers and Saints, giving us hope they were rounding into form and becoming something more than the mediocrity we had seen for nearly a decade running. Those hopes are not entirely dashed, but they are certainly dimmed by the past two games. Facing good coaches and good teams, the Falcons have stumbled. Last week they played a close, solid game that fell apart late against the Ravens with a backup quarterback, and this week they managed to turn a 31-7 game into a 31-23 game late. Notably in both cases, they lost owing to excruciating special teams mishaps, defensive lapses spurred by injuries, and whatever the hell has been going on offensively. That has taken them from 2-2 to 2-4, hovering just above the dismal basement of the NFC South, and has effectively blown a hole in all the arguments for taking them seriously. Did you believe in the offense? They’ve been weirdly allergic to Bijan Robinson early in games and their quarterback, while capable of brilliance, is faltering under pressure. Do you love the defense? It’s down multiple cornerbacks, both starting linebackers, and is showing the cracks you’d expect when major injuries pile up. Did you have high hopes for special teams after an encouraging summer? They have a massive, persistent return game problem that has repeatedly put the offense in bad spots and given opposing teams life. And so on. Against a very good Bears that punched above its weight defensively for much of the afternoon, this team was only intermittently competitive. They were within one score early but kept dropping further and further behind until they were down 31-7, at which point the defense got a couple of stops, the offense kicked into high gear, and they climbed back within eight. After the team’s last ditch drive fell short, the defense couldn’t keep the Bears from running out the clock and they dropped their third game in three tries at home this year. There’s a wide swath of blame to go around here, and what makes efforts like these even more frustrating is that this team can pull together stretches of something approaching excellence, but has been unable to sustain them these past two weeks. Look, this is a team with a clear laundry list of needs, a massive amount of 2027 cap space, and enough picks to potentially go out and grab the high end players they need to fill those holes, and generally the decisions the front office has made to this point encourage us to feel hopeful about the future. item.content:encoded: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 18: Bijan Robinson #7 of the Atlanta Falcons rushes during the first quarter against the Chicago Bears at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons turned in two glorious weeks where they beat down the Packers and Saints, giving us hope they were rounding into form and becoming something more than the mediocrity we had seen for nearly a decade running. Those hopes are not entirely dashed, but they are certainly dimmed by the past two games. Facing good coaches and good teams, the Falcons have stumbled. Last week they played a close, solid game that fell apart late against the Ravens with a backup quarterback, and this week they managed to turn a 31-7 game into a 31-23 game late. Notably in both cases, they lost owing to excruciating special teams mishaps, defensive lapses spurred by injuries, and whatever the hell has been going on offensively. That has taken them from 2-2 to 2-4, hovering just above the dismal basement of the NFC South, and has effectively blown a hole in all the arguments for taking them seriously. Did you believe in the offense? They’ve been weirdly allergic to Bijan Robinson early in games and their quarterback, while capable of brilliance, is faltering under pressure. Do you love the defense? It’s down multiple cornerbacks, both starting linebackers, and is showing the cracks you’d expect when major injuries pile up. Did you have high hopes for special teams after an encouraging summer? They have a massive, persistent return game problem that has repeatedly put the offense in bad spots and given opposing teams life. And so on. Against a very good Bears that punched above its weight defensively for much of the afternoon, this team was only intermittently competitive. They were within one score early but kept dropping further and further behind until they were down 31-7, at which point the defense got a couple of stops, the offense kicked into high gear, and they climbed back within eight. After the team’s last ditch drive fell short, the defense couldn’t keep the Bears from running out the clock and they dropped their third game in three tries at home this year. There’s a wide swath of blame to go around here, and what makes efforts like these even more frustrating is that this team can pull together stretches of something approaching excellence, but has been unable to sustain them these past two weeks. Look, this is a team with a clear laundry list of needs, a massive amount of 2027 cap space, and enough picks to potentially go out and grab the high end players they need to fill those holes, and generally the decisions the front office has made to this point encourage us to feel hopeful about the future. If you came into this season expecting an up-and-down first season for Kevin Stefanski and company, the broad contours of this season to this point aren’t shocking. We probably need to retain the capacity to look at the future in a reasonable way to endure the roller coaster we are most assuredly riding now. We should also remember that outside of that dismal effort against the Panthers, the Falcons have been competitive in every game they’ve played despite the many rookies and one-year signings they’re relying on to get the job done in 2026, which is worth something . But! The here and now is deeply frustrating. It’s hard to explain why Bijan Robinson had one carry in the first two drives against a weak run defense and only nine carries overall when he’s so dynamic that he can change the flow of a game, even if you’re down by a lot. It’s hard to watch this team’s returners repeatedly elect to make a go at it with punts and kicks they have no business fielding and believe there’s not a ton of work to be done in that phase. And it’s hard to see such a game effort from a bruised and battered defense—please get well soon, Kendal Daniels—undone by injuries and other phases of the game, especially when they’re having to contend with Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams. It is just frustrating to be a Falcons fans right now, as it long has been, and difficult to see them reversing this skid against a 49ers team that ranks among the NFL’s best next week. Too long this team has been defined by what it can’t do rather than what it can do, and if the ceiling feels a bit higher this year with the glimpses of great play we’ve seen, the downside still seems destined to define their 2026. At 2-4, they’ll need to prove that sentiment wrong in a hurry if they’re able to do so. On to the full recap. The Good Michael Penix seems destined to be in both The Good and The Ugly every week with the way things are tracking. The good is not difficult to see—Penix got going against the blitz in the second half, he made some tremendous throws to Jahan Dotson, Kyle Pitts, and Drake London along the way—and I’m hopeful that him going out there and slinging three touchdowns after exiting last week with a rib injury will quiet some of the unjustified criticism of his toughness. When you can keep him clean or he knows where the pressure is coming from, Penix can do tremendous things. Bijan Robinson did well with his limited touches, with the only (very real) blemish on his day coming in the form of a rough holding call. The shame is that he didn’t get more work. It was another fine day from Drake London, who hoovered up every target he had a reasonable chance at, but this was the Kyle Pitts breakout game. He reeled in five of his seven targets for 60 yards and a pair of touchdowns, both excellent efforts and one of which saw him extend to make the score happen. After a three week drought to start the season that saw him with just two grabs for 20 yards on six targets, Pitts has 13 grabs for 149 yards and three touchdowns over the past three weeks. Tommy Rees appears to be figuring out how to utilize him, and if the team can just do so more consistently earlier in games, the offense should be in better shape. I’ve had Jahan Dotson in a dynasty league for a while now, so I’ve tracked his career with interest and have long felt he was better than his production has indicated. I was a fan of dropping him into this offense given his ability to win deep, and we saw that in Weeks 4 and 5. What we hadn’t seen necessarily was the ability to win contested catches, but Dotson did that on a great touchdown grab against the Bears where he was blanketed but reeled in a pretty ball from Michael Penix Jr. for the score, and Dotson finished as the team’s leading receiver with 87 yards and a score on three grabs. The one where he came back on an underthrown Penix deep ball and spun out of a tackle to pick up additional yardage afterwards was also worth calling out. The team needed a non-London receiving threat to step up, and Dotson is doing it in a major way. That Gervon Dexter/Brandon Dorlus duo is as good as it gets. They were one of the few consistent sources of pressure in this one and came up with two of Atlanta’s four sacks, with LaCale London and Za’Darius Smith also chipping in one each. All four have been assets this year, but Dorlus and Dexter simply blow up pockets week after week and even made a quarterback as elusive as Caleb Williams uncomfortable. Jessie Bates forced a fumble, the second straight week he’s been involved in a big turnover, with Harold Perkins Jr. scooping the ball up. After a quiet start to the year, Bates is heating up. I give Harold Perkins Jr. and Josh Woods a lot of credit for needing to come into this game and play major snaps with Divine Deablo and Kendal Daniels both out and holding their own, particularly Woods given that his role is typically exclusively on special teams. While special teams has been something of a disaster for Atlanta in 2026, it’s not because of Jake Bailey. The punter absolutely boomed multiple punts today despite unfavorable field position, giving Atlanta’s defense a fighting chance, and has bee

item.title: Bears rebound with explosive offense in win over Falcons
item.description: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 18: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears celebrates a touchdown against the Atlanta Falcons during the first quarter of the game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears needed a statement win with Caleb Williams coming back from injury and the team having just suffered a tough loss to the Packers the week before. With their matchup against the Falcons on Sunday, they found exactly that. The 31-23 score isn’t quite reflective of how the game went for most of the time. Atlanta was able to score 16 points in the fourth quarter, partially due to Ben Johnson’s decision to put in his defensive backups early in the quarter, giving the Falcons more time to eat into the lead. But that snafu aside, this was a game that the Bears dominated a vast majority of the time. Offensively and defensively, Chicago was the better team. As the Bears move to 4-2 for the season, here are some of my takeaways from the game. Caleb returns with a vengeance After missing three games with a hamstring injury, Caleb Williams made his long-awaited return to the field on Sunday. Upon first review, he didn’t have a single incompletion that wasn’t a throwaway. That’s an absurd level of efficiency. He finished the game going 30-for-36 (83.3%) with 305 passing yards, a touchdown, no interceptions, and a 111.2 passer rating. His accuracy helped elevated the Bears’ offense to a strong performance against the Falcons’ defense. As of this writing, Williams’ 80.6 initial PFN QB Impact grade ranked No. 4 among all NFL quarterbacks in Week 6. Most advanced analytics had him as at least a top-five quarterback for the week, and he ranks No. 6 in the league in the aforementioned PFN QB Impact grade throughout the entire season. His ability to play on time within Ben Johnson’s offense has been remarkable in the two non-monsoon games he’s played, and his confidence and poise stood out on Sunday. Dennis Allen’s stellar three quarters The 23 points that the Bears gave up are not entirely reflective of how their defense performed over most of the game. Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen did a great job of manufacturing pressure up front, as Michael Penix Jr. ended up sacked five times on Sunday. Three of those sacks came from Kyler Gordon, who had three sacks and five quick pressures on just eight pass-rushing snaps. Allen has done a great job of using the blitz to make up for a lack of pressure from a four-man rush, and his consistent looks of double-mug A-gap blitzes, only to drop certain defenders back in coverage, have kept quarterbacks guessing snap after snap. Gordon has been a tremendous blitzing defensive back during his time with the Bears, and as Allen has taken a blitz-heavy approach to calling plays, Gordon’s physicality and urgency has been a tremendous fit. He looked right at home in his first game of the 2026 season. Avoiding catastrophe is a sign of growth As

(Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears needed a statement win with Caleb Williams coming back from injury and the team having just suffered a tough loss to the Packers the week before. With their matchup against the Falcons on Sunday, they found exactly that. The 31-23 score isn’t quite reflective of how the game went for most of the time. Atlanta was able to score 16 points in the fourth quarter, partially due to Ben Johnson’s decision to put in his defensive backups early in the quarter, giving the Falcons more time to eat into the lead. But that snafu aside, this was a game that the Bears dominated a vast majority of the time. Offensively and defensively, Chicago was the better team. As the Bears move to 4-2 for the season, here are some of my takeaways from the game. Caleb returns with a vengeance After missing three games with a hamstring injury, Caleb Williams made his long-awaited return to the field on Sunday. Upon first review, he didn’t have a single incompletion that wasn’t a throwaway. That’s an absurd level of efficiency. He finished the game going 30-for-36 (83.3%) with 305 passing yards, a touchdown, no interceptions, and a 111.2 passer rating. His accuracy helped elevated the Bears’ offense to a strong performance against the Falcons’ defense. As of this writing, Williams’ 80.6 initial PFN QB Impact grade ranked No. 4 among all NFL quarterbacks in Week 6. Most advanced analytics had him as at least a top-five quarterback for the week, and he ranks No. 6 in the league in the aforementioned PFN QB Impact grade throughout the entire season. His ability to play on time within Ben Johnson’s offense has been remarkable in the two non-monsoon games he’s played, and his confidence and poise stood out on Sunday. Dennis Allen’s stellar three quarters The 23 points that the Bears gave up are not entirely reflective of how their defense performed over most of the game. Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen did a great job of manufacturing pressure up front, as Michael Penix Jr. ended up sacked five times on Sunday. Three of those sacks came from Kyler Gordon, who had three sacks and five quick pressures on just eight pass-rushing snaps. Allen has done a great job of using the blitz to make up for a lack of pressure from a four-man rush, and his consistent looks of double-mug A-gap blitzes, only to drop certain defenders back in coverage, have kept quarterbacks guessing snap after snap. Gordon has been a tremendous blitzing defensive back during his time with the Bears, and as Allen has taken a blitz-heavy approach to calling plays, Gordon’s physicality and urgency has been a tremendous fit. He looked right at home in his first game of the 2026 season. Avoiding catastrophe is a sign of growth As a head coach, there haven’t been too many games where Ben Johnson has had to protect a massive lead. Any Bears fan will tell you that many of their matchups in that electric 2025 season often came down to the wire, with Chicago either playing from behind or engaged in an evenly-matched shootout until the very end. The Bears held a massive lead over the Falcons going into the fourth quarter, and though they almost gave it up, they didn’t collapse. Is that a low bar to reach? Potentially. But the Bears have had so many blown leads over the years under previous head coaches, and for a moment, Sunday’s finish felt like another instance of the team falling apart in the final stretch. When Kyler Gordon had that strip sack on third down to give the Bears the ball with three minutes left in regulation, and the offense was able to kill the clock with a well-executed run game, some of those demons became exercised. As Johnson becomes more comfortable with a big lead, it would be surprising to see him take his foot off the gas as much as he did on Sunday. It was a great learning experience, and Chicago picked up the slack before it was too late.

item.title: First Glance: Alabama
item.description: TUSCALOOSA, ALABAMA - SEPTEMBER 26: Alabama Crimson Tide mascot Big Al works the crowd with the cheerleaders prior to kickoff of the game against the South Carolina Gamecocks at Bryant-Denny Stadium on September 26, 2026 in Tuscaloosa, Alabama. (Photo by Jason Clark/Getty Images) | Getty Images Get to Know Alabama: Location: Tuscaloosa, AL Established: 1820 Enrollment: 42,360 Mascot: Crimson Tide Colors: Crimson and white Conference: SEC (duh) What You Need to Know: Texas A&M is 4-3 (1-3) and coming off of a (pretty meaningless) 41-0 win over The Citadel Alabama is 5-2 (3-2), coming off of two straight losses vs Georgia and at Tennessee. There aren’t may reasons to expect the Aggies to be competitive in this game. But then again, competing against Bama when nobody expected us to has kinda been our thing in recent seasons. Betting Lines: Texas A&M is a 15.5-point underdog . The over/under is 50.5. Historical Notes: Alabama leads the all-time series 13-3, and leads 10-2 since the Aggies joined the SEC. This is the first time the Aggies have played Alabama since the retirement of Nick Saban Famous Alabama alumni include To Kill a Mockingbird author Harper Lee, Wikipedia co-founder Jimmy Wales, actors Sela Ward and Jim Nabors, Lady Bird Johnson, Dabo Swinney, Paul “Bear” Bryant, golfer Justin Thomas and College Gameday host Rece Davis. What To Watch For: Defensive improvement. Don’t look now, but Texas A&M’s pass defense is ranked No. 10 nationally. There’s some context to that, to be sure (giving up a lot on the ground and also some really subpar opponents), but the defense has looked like it’s been rounding into form after some pretty obvious early-season struggles. They’ll need to continue that upward trajectory and then some if they hope to pull out a victory this Saturday. Any offense at all. Against LSU and Missouri, the A&M offense looked simply abysmal, failing to even score a touchdown. It may seem silly to expect significant improvement at this point (it is), but it’s what it will take for A&M to have a shot in this game. Health? Texas A&M rested a number of players last week, with starters like WR Mario Craver, OG Trovon Baugh, DE Anto Saka and DT DJ Hicks not even suiting up. Will that rest prove fruitful against a Crimson Tide team coming off of games against Georgia and Tennessee? It’s a stretch, but hey, it could happen (flaps arms in a forced Angels in the Outfield reference). Media Blitz: Venue: Bryant-Denny Stadium (Tuscaloosa, AL) Kickoff: 2:30 p.m. Saturday, Oct. 24 TV: ABC Weather: High 76°F | Low 45°F — Partly sunny with a low rain chance (5%–10%)

item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PA - SEPTEMBER 22: Luis Arraez #4 of the Philadelphia Phillies warms up during batting practice prior to the game between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Philadelphia Phillies at Citizens Bank Park on Tuesday, September 22, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Denis Kennedy/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images If the Cardinals want to compete next season, it would be wise to shore up their positions of weakness. The bullpen is a clear weakness, but it’s also the part of the team I would probably focus on last personally. An argument for the best closer in baseball is Bryan Baker of the Tampa Bay Rays, a 31-year-old with 3 career saves entering this season. Baker was drafted by the Rockies, traded as the player to be named later in a package for a year and a month of Seung Hwan Oh, selected off waivers by the Orioles a few years later, and finally traded for a draft pick last deadline. Meanwhile, Edwin Diaz got paid $17 million to allow nearly a run per inning in his 21 appearances for the Dodgers. Neither of these are unusual stories for relievers. So most of my offseason talk will be focused on finding someone for either third base, center field, or starting pitcher. There is a very big, unfortunate issue with this however: the free agent market at those positions kind of suck. It’s why my very first free agent profile was focused on someone who has barely played 3B (JP Crawford). Any true 3B upgrade will either have to come via trade or someone at a different position. Which brings me to today’s post. In theory, anybody who plays second base can play third base. And while that is literally true, the two positions require different strengths so they are likely not going provide the same quality of defense. But the truth of the matter is that the 2B market is significantly stronger than the 3B market. At the very least entertaining the better second basemen on the market is worth exploring to improve 3B. You could also move JJ Wetherholt to 3B, but I am opposed to that, so I would make it clear to these free agents that they would have to play 3B. It’d be an easier argument because Wetherholt is indeed better defensively than every other 2B. So if for no other reason than to eliminate them as real targets, let’s look at the 2B who might make sense at 3B.
