item.content:encoded: PHILADELPHIA, PA - SEPTEMBER 22: Luis Arraez #4 of the Philadelphia Phillies warms up during batting practice prior to the game between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Philadelphia Phillies at Citizens Bank Park on Tuesday, September 22, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Denis Kennedy/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images If the Cardinals want to compete next season, it would be wise to shore up their positions of weakness. The bullpen is a clear weakness, but it’s also the part of the team I would probably focus on last personally. An argument for the best closer in baseball is Bryan Baker of the Tampa Bay Rays, a 31-year-old with 3 career saves entering this season. Baker was drafted by the Rockies, traded as the player to be named later in a package for a year and a month of Seung Hwan Oh, selected off waivers by the Orioles a few years later, and finally traded for a draft pick last deadline. Meanwhile, Edwin Diaz got paid $17 million to allow nearly a run per inning in his 21 appearances for the Dodgers. Neither of these are unusual stories for relievers. So most of my offseason talk will be focused on finding someone for either third base, center field, or starting pitcher. There is a very big, unfortunate issue with this however: the free agent market at those positions kind of suck. It’s why my very first free agent profile was focused on someone who has barely played 3B (JP Crawford). Any true 3B upgrade will either have to come via trade or someone at a different position. Which brings me to today’s post. In theory, anybody who plays second base can play third base. And while that is literally true, the two positions require different strengths so they are likely not going provide the same quality of defense. But the truth of the matter is that the 2B market is significantly stronger than the 3B market. At the very least entertaining the better second basemen on the market is worth exploring to improve 3B. You could also move JJ Wetherholt to 3B, but I am opposed to that, so I would make it clear to these free agents that they would have to play 3B. It’d be an easier argument because Wetherholt is indeed better defensively than every other 2B. So if for no other reason than to eliminate them as real targets, let’s look at the 2B who might make sense at 3B. Brandon Lowe 2026 Stats: .260/.331/.493, 9.5 BB%, 28.8 K%, .233 ISO, .319 BABIP, 121 wRC+, 4.9 fWAR Expected Deal: 4 years, $70 million The Tampa Bay Rays are one win away from the World Series. They also, at least as of now, made an extremely bad trade involving Brandon Lowe. They traded one season of Lowe, getting paid $11.5 million, 5 seasons of Mason Montgomery (2.2 fWAR out of the bullpen), and Jake Magnum (who isn’t very good) for 25-year-old Jacob Melton (who missed most of 2026 to injury and never saw the majors) and Anderson Brito, a mediocre prospect who only pitched in 8 games in 2026 at a level he had already pitched before (and he was worse at that level in 2026). With all that said, Brandon Lowe has more warning signs than a radiation plant. He will most likely receive a qualified offer, and that is not a good start. In his previous four seasons prior to 2026, he averaged under 2 WAR per season. He was randomly great at defense after a career of not being very good defensively. The first year of his deal will be at 32-years-old. And he has never played an inning of 3B at pro ball. Also his arm is 11th percentile according to Statcast, though 2B hold back more than 3B as we will soon see. The arm is the big one because frankly, a career of being not great defensively is actually a very good argument for someone to move to 3B. But I wanted to take a one-year game on Crawford defensively, and you would likely be taking a 3-4 year gamble on Lowe (his QO could very much hurt his market to an extreme degree though). On the positive side, his power wouldn’t be that terribly affected by Busch. He hit 35 homers for the Pirates. It would have been 32 at Busch. But unfortunately, I have even more warning signs. For as good of a season as he had, there are so many reasons to not sign this guy. My last warning sign is that his offense looked to be on the luckier side. He had his highest K% since 2019 and he had his highest BABIP also since 2019. That’s not a great combo. His xwOBA was .331, which was his lowest since 2022 in his injury-shortened season. His actual wOBA was .354. I’m going to be completely honest. I think I would avoid Lowe even if the Cardinals had a hole at 2B. A 32-year-old who probably didn’t actually get better last season but saw a career year saddled with a QO? And we have to move him to 3B, a position he hasn’t played professionally, and he has a weak arm? Conclusion: Avoid Luis Arraez 2026: .310/.345/.419, 5.2 BB%, 4.3 K%, .109 ISO, .311 BABIP, 110 wRC+, 4.1 fWAR Expected Contract: I don’t think I can even guess, I have no idea The great big mystery of Arraez is how does the league value Arraez? Coming off a 0.9 fWAR season, Arraez signed for $1 year, $12 million. That is honestly more than most 0.9 WAR players will get, maybe all of them, so I’m not necessarily taking it as a given that the league doesn’t value Arraez like anti-stats people like to say. He will be 30-years-old and will likely get a multi-year deal. With that said, his offense did not really get that much better, he was a significantly better player because he was suddenly great at defense. I have not looked into why, but unlike Lowe who was generally below average before 2026, Arraez was straight up awful defensively. Even with genuine improvements, it’s very hard to buy into his 2026 level of defense. You just don’t really see that kind of jump defensively, ever, and if it was hitting that did it, everyone would be similarly skeptical. When a sudden jump happens, you don’t assume the same level, you go somewhere in between where he used to be and his career year. Arraez has played 3B, although very little, and like 2B and like 1B, he was awful defensively. I don’t think his arm is an issue. It’s 25th percentile, but I think he has more in the tank. When he last played significant innings at 3B, he threw it four miles per hour harder at 3B than when he played at 2B. And his arm at 2B this past season was very similar to how hard he threw at 2B in the year he also played 3B. He was actually dead average the year he played 400 innings at 3B, for some reason he was -7 OAA in 40 innings the very next season and nobody’s tried him at 3B since. His bat is more reliable, although not near as good as the batting average people think. He doesn’t walk and he has no power, so he’s an above average hitter, but definitely not elite. He also hits into a lot of double plays. He hit into 15 double plays last season and has averaged just about that in the last four seasons. He somehow hit into 18 double plays when he batted .354. As I said in the beginning, I don’t really know how the league values him. My interest in him is entirely dependent on his next contract. Is he valued like an All-Star, because I’d definitely avoid that contract. Like the 1 WAR player he was in 2024 and 2025? That means short-term and that’s more interesting. Conclusion: Probably not Jazz Chisholm 2026: .231/.321/.399, 10.5 BB%, 29.5 K%, .168 ISO, .301 BABIP, 98 wRC+, 3.5 fWAR Expected Contract: 4 years, $80 million Chisholm is kind of the opposite of our first two choices. His 2026 season stats are him coming off a down season and he’s very likely good on defense, despite his blunders. His numbers at 3B are a bit of a mixed bag – he was very good in 2024 and not good in 2025, and then the Yankees stopped playing him at 3B. He’s similar to Arraez in that he threw it harder at 3B than he does at 2B and most of his 9th percentile arm is related to that fact. He threw it 85.6 mph at 3B last year, 78.5 mph at 2B. So he must be really having his fair share of lobbing it over at 2B. It’

item.title: Texas football mailbag: What changes is Steve Sarkisian willing to make after two straight losses?
item.description: Steve Sarkisian said he would evaluate "everything" after Texas' second straight loss to an unranked team. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) AUSTIN - Another week, and another unsightly Texas loss , prompts plenty of questions from readers, more than we can fit into our weekly Longhorn newsletter . So here's a crack at answering your questions about Steve Sarkisian, Arch Manning and what troubles Texas football . Q: If you were Sark, what changes would you make to at least have a chance to beat Ole Miss? KB: Bench Manning. Let A.J. Milwee call the plays. Ask the offensive line to please block somebody. Ask the NCAA to make blitzing illegal because Texas can't handle it and apparently has never seen it before. That's all for now. Q: How long before (athletic director) Chris Del Conte gives Sark the ultimatum …. let someone else call the plays? And what happened to blitzing the QB? Did Will Muschamp get stupid after he got back to Austin? - John W. KB: He should give it to him today. Or yesterday. Sarkisian had better realize he needs to give that part of the game up. After all, he said he fired Pete Kwiatkowski so he could solely focus on the offense. If Texas doesn't make the CFP, I would bet the administration would politely suggest - OK, demand - the head coach make changes. I don't know why Muschamp doesn't blitz more. We aren't allowed to talk to him. Sign up for Kirk Bohls' newsletter Sign up for Kirk Bohls' new newsletter for news, exclusive analysis and insights on University of Texas sports. Q: Frequently, the Longhorns begin to fade in the third quarter. Are they being outcoached at halftime? It appears that the opponents identify Longhorn weaknesses and make changes at halftime. - Joe Dahlstrom KB: Yes, they are being outcoached. Clearly. End of story. Q: What are the odds that Sarkisian will give QB2 a shot? I think Arch Manning is a good QB, but after a year and a half as a starter, I see very little improvement. Arch is not bad, he's just not consistent. Neither is an offensive line that appears confused and out of sync. Certainly the Texas staff must feel they are squandering a very talented class? - The Real Bunky KB: None of us see any improvement in Manning. If someone has, please let me know. He's had three critical turnovers in the fourth quarter in the past two games. That cannot happen. The offensive line is terrible. Q: I have an idea, bench Sarkisian for his play-calling. Either get a new offensive coach or a new coach. Sarkisian seems intent to show everyone what a good play-caller he is. During the game he never even talks to his players, especially Arch. This is not right. He still has not done anything about the offensive line! Either he changes his ways or get a new coach. - Sharolyn Wagner KB: He hasn't done anything about the offensive line because he kept Kyle Flood. Other than Kelvin Banks, the line hasn't been good since Sark got here. Q: Would any other quarterback have been pulled (benched) for his i

item.title: Morning Report | Farid Basharat responds to Dana White saying there’s ‘a reason’ he wasn’t re-signed to the UFC
item.description: Farid Basharat | ﻿Photo by Cooper Neill/Zuffa LLC) Farid Basharat does not agree with Dana White. Last week, Basharat’s time in the UFC ended when the undefeated fighter was not re-signed to the promotion after completing his UFC contract. This caused quite the stir as Basharat was a ranked bantamweight and had a sterling 7-0 record in the UFC. Following UFC Edmonton on Saturday, UFC CEO Dana White was asked why Basharat was not re-signed to the promotion, with White cryptically responding that “there’s definitely a reason” why the UFC parted ways with him, pointing out that in similar previous instances, it’s usually been because a fighter was hard to deal. Well, on Sunday, Basharat responded to White’s claims on his social media, rejecting the implication entirely. “I just want to address these comments made by Dana at the press conference last night. First of all, he kind of alluded to maybe I was turning down fights, or maybe I was difficult to deal with. “First of all, and I’ve said this many times already, I definitely didn’t turn nobody down. In fact, we’re talking about the same guy that, in Abu Dhabi when I fought in 2024, my opponent missed weight by 10 pounds and I still went ahead with the fight. And from what I know, it’s the largest weight disparity in UFC history. Still went ahead with the fight, still put on a good show, and won. My Contender Series fight, I had a torn MCL in my elbow, still went ahead with the fight. “So, these are facts you can ask your UFC staff, you can ask the nutrition team, you can ask the physio team. They will tell you these are facts. And with regards to if I was difficult to deal with, again, speak to your staff. Ask anybody about me, there was no issues with me in any way, shape, or form. “I just feel like I had to put that out there, just to almost clear my name, because Dana’s gone out there and said all these things. In all my fights, my opponent had a combined record of, I think, 20-6. They’d only been finished once. And to go out there, I beat them all, I always put on a good show, every single one of my last three opponents I rocked or hurt. I just feel like I had to make this video to kind of almost clear things up.” In a separate video posted to his YouTube account prior to White’s statement, Basharat also went into detail about how his UFC tenure ended and why he believes it happened. “UFC 329 in July, that was my final fight on the contract,” Basharat said. “It was my fourth fight on my second contract. Generally, how it works in the UFC, before you fight your last fight out, you try to sit down with the organization and try and get a renewal going. “We went through with the fight; obviously, I got the victory, and then subsequently after that we reached out to say, ‘Let’s renegotiate.’ They kind of stalled, just kind of put the talks on hold. And essentially, I didn’t hear anything from the UFC for about three months. I fought mid-July, and by the time I got the news was the end of October.

They will tell you these are facts. And with regards to if I was difficult to deal with, again, speak to your staff. Ask anybody about me, there was no issues with me in any way, shape, or form. “I just feel like I had to put that out there, just to almost clear my name, because Dana’s gone out there and said all these things. In all my fights, my opponent had a combined record of, I think, 20-6. They’d only been finished once. And to go out there, I beat them all, I always put on a good show, every single one of my last three opponents I rocked or hurt. And essentially, I didn’t hear anything from the UFC for about three months. I fought mid-July, and by the time I got the news was the end of October. So, over three months I didn’t really hear from them.” “I don’t think I fit the direction that they’re trying to move in,” Basharat continued. “I think they’re trying to go for brawlers, spill your blood whether you win or lose type of stuff. And me, the way I fight, it’s high IQ, intelligent, defeat the opponent where they’re weak, and don’t fight them where they’re strong. And I don’t think that’s what they’re going for. … “I think the company, the UFC, is manufacturing a fanbase that doesn’t appreciate good quality fighting, and they just appreciate these rock’em type fights where, even if it’s a mismatch, even if it’s a low-level fight, as long as there’s blood, as long as it’s a first-round finish, we’re happy. And in my opinion, you can’t build a sport off that. You might do well for a couple of years ratings-wise, but sooner or later, it’s going to delegitimize the sport.” TOP STORIES Dreams. item.title: 5 things we learned from the Chiefs’ Week 6 victory over the Chargers
item.description: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Coming off the bye, the Kansas City Chiefs entered this game looking to go 3-0 against AFC West opponents this season. It was evident from the jump who the better team was. The Chiefs didn’t play a perfect game, and at times it felt like they were coasting, but they dominated all four quarters. Kansas City’s pass rushers and standout running back Kenneth Walker III were especially impressive in the Chiefs’ 22-6 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers . Here are five things we learned from the Chiefs stealing the Chargers’ lunch money: 1. K9 is not just the top dog; he’s the NFL MVP Through the first six weeks of the season, this isn’t even up for debate. I know the NFL decided in some nefarious back-channel meeting that the NFL MVP is now a quarterback award. The only exception is when a running back is having a truly transcendent year—well, Kenneth Walker III is doing just that. Over five games, Walker has 665 rushing yards and averages 6.2 yards per carry, with eight total touchdowns. For reference, the last time a non-quarterback won the NFL MVP was in 2012 when Minnesota Vikings running back Adrian Peterson won the award. That season, Peterson rushed for 2,097 yards and 13 total touchdowns, averaging six yards per carry. Before Peterson won the award, you have to go back to 2006 to find the next season a non-quarterback won the MVP. Chargers running back LaDainian Tomlinson won that year. Interestingly, in 2005, Seattle Seahawks running back Shaun Alexander also won MVP. In 2006, Tomlinson ran for 1,815 yards and 31 total touchdowns, averaging 5.2 yards per carry. In 2005, Alexander ran 1,880 yards and 28 total touchdowns, averaging 5.1 yards per carry. It’s still early, and Walker needs to keep up this pace and stay healthy for the rest of the season, but right now, Walker is on pace to rush for 2,260 yards and 27 total touchdowns. Those numbers would not only surpass Peterson’s 2012 MVP campaign, but also beat Los Angeles Rams Eric Dickerson’s all-time single-season rushing record of 2,105 yards that has stood since 1984. Even more impressive. He’s on pace for 2,583 all-purpose yards, which would also beat Tennessee Titans running back Chris Johnson’s 2009 record of 2,509 yards, Walker isn’t just on pace for a great season; he’s on pace for the greatest season of any running back in NFL history. Kenneth Walker III kept rolling with another huge game for Kansas City. 19 CAR, 128 RUSH YDS, 6.7 YPC, 2 TD, 2 REC, 11 REC YDS Walker continues to build a serious OPOY case in his first season with the Chiefs. pic.twitter.com/H7UDopZeHW https://t.co/g2cWBUkgRc — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) October 18, 2026 2. Chiefs are the Kings of the West It feels good to be back on the throne. With this victory over the Chargers, the Chiefs have ensured they will have at least a .500 record against AFC West opponents this season. Interestingly, in 2005, Seattle Seahawks running back Shaun Alexander also won MVP. In 2006, Tomlinson ran for 1,815 yards and 31 total touchdowns, averaging 5.2 yards per carry. In 2005, Alexander ran 1,880 yards and 28 total touchdowns, averaging 5.1 yards per carry. It’s still early, and Walker needs to keep up this pace and stay healthy for the rest of the season, but right now, Walker is on pace to rush for 2,260 yards and 27 total touchdowns. Those numbers would not only surpass Peterson’s 2012 MVP campaign, but also beat Los Angeles Rams Eric Dickerson’s all-time single-season rushing record of 2,105 yards that has stood since 1984. Even more impressive. He’s on pace for 2,583 all-purpose yards, which would also beat Tennessee Titans running back Chris Johnson’s 2009 record of 2,509 yards, Walker isn’t just on pace for a great season; he’s on pace for the greatest season of any running back in NFL history. Kenneth Walker III kept rolling with another huge game for Kansas City. 19 CAR, 128 RUSH YDS, 6.7 YPC, 2 TD, 2 REC, 11 REC YDS Walker continues to build a serious OPOY case in his first season with the Chiefs. pic.twitter.com/H7UDopZeHW https://t.co/g2cWBUkgRc — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) October 18, 2026 2. Chiefs are the Kings of the West It feels good to be back on the throne. With this victory over the Chargers, the Chiefs have ensured they will have at least a .500 record against AFC West opponents this season. With the Las Vegas Raiders losing to the Buffalo Bills , the Raiders are 3-3, and the Denver Broncos are the Chiefs’ next closest opponents at 4-2. But let’s be honest: after watching Bo Nix’s ineptitude and the rest of Denver’s offense, do you really think they have what it takes to catch up with the Chiefs? As for the Chargers, they look like the worst team in the NFL. No, they look worse than bad. They look cursed. Sports have a long history of cursed franchises. The reasons a franchise might be cursed range from how fans treat it to trading a legendary player. In the Chargers case, I’m going to jump to an unfounded conclusion and say it’s because they left San Diego. They are being punished from the great beyond by a spirit who is angry they relocated to Los Angeles. San Diego loved that franchise, and they left it for the bright lights of Hollywood. The only question is, whose spirit is responsible for tormenting them? Personally, as a Chiefs fan, I hope it’s Marty Schottenheimer. 3. Nikko Remigio is not as dependable as we were told We were told Nikko Remigio was the Chiefs’ kick and punt returner because he was dependable and does not put the ball on the ground. Well, that changed in this game. He fumbled once and nearly fumbled again, but he was saved because he was down by a hair. The Chiefs also had a block in the back on the play where Remigio fumbled. Harrison Butker missed a point-after attempt and has only made 25% of his attempts from 50+ yards. It doesn’t matter if you can kick the ball a mile if you can’t kick it straight. Not a great day for Harrison Butker. Good from 44, misses wide right from 52, and missed a PAT. — Matt Derrick (@mattderrick) October 18, 2026 4. A bad offensive line makes your pass rush look awesome Chiefs edge rusher George Karlaftis brought his hardhat and lunchpail to work today, and proceeded to abuse the Chargers’ battered offensive line. In fact, nearly everyone joined in on the fun of bullying the human-shaped cutouts the Chargers propped up in front of Justin Herbert. Ashton Gillotte, Peter Woods, and Felix Anudike-Uzomah all hit the quarterback. And just like their last game against the Raiders, when the Chiefs needed somebody to step up and close out the game, the pass rush showed up, with R Mason Thomas beating his man around the edge and hitting Justin Herbert’s arm as he threw. Chiefs edge rushers today: – George Karlaftis: 26.3% pressure rate, 2.33 time to pressure, 1 sack, 2 TFLs – R Mason Thomas: 20.8% pressure rate, 2.31 time to pressure — SūmerSports (@SumerSports) October 19, 2026 5. The Chiefs need Josh Simmons Not because the offensive line played bad today. On the contrary, I thought it was one of their better games this season. But they also took their lumps. Right tackle Jaylon Moore left the game with a concussion. Left guard Suamataia had a calf stinger. Diego Pounds has been inactive all season. But even if fully healthy, the Chiefs didn’t have much depth on the offensive line. Despite playing admirably, I don’t feel great about the Chiefs running out Kahlil Benson and Joshua Ezeudu for a full four quarters against the Seahawks next week. Trying to tackle Kenneth Walker does NOT look fun pic.twitter.com/FtfvsQo2g1 — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) October 4, 2026

item.title: Detroit Tigers News: Willie Horton, MLB Postseason, Rays, Guardians, Dodgers, Drew Rasmussen
item.description: CLEVELAND, OHIO - OCTOBER 18: PitcherDrew Rasmussen #57 of the Tampa Bay Rays celebrates at the end of the first inning against the Cleveland Guardians in game five of the American League Championship Series at Progressive Field on October 18, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Happy Monday, everyone! We could know as soon as tonight who will be heading to the World Series against the Brewers, or whether we’ll get a nail-biter Game 7 in the ALCS. Today we’ll check in on how the Rays have managed to turn things around when they needed it the most, and how pitcher Drew Rasmussen came in clutch precisely when his team needed him. We round things up with some postseason chatter as well as some offseason and free agency overview. Plus, the Tigers have added a new member to their coaching staff, and it’s a reunion of sorts for A.J. Hinch from his Astros days. Let’s get right into it. Detroit Tigers News Happy Willie Horton Day! One of the greatest to ever wear the Olde English D and #RepDetroit Join us in celebrating Willie Horton’s 84th birthday and Willie Horton Day in the state of Michigan! 👏 pic.twitter.com/JWyh5IXClE — Detroit Tigers (@tigers) October 18, 2026 Bros supporting bros. pic.twitter.com/i2I9fDqx1J — Detroit Tigers (@tigers) October 16, 2026 A new addition to the Tigers coaching staff. Longtime MLB catcher Martín Maldonado is in agreement to join the Detroit Tigers coaching staff, sources tell @CodyStavenhagen and me – https://t.co/QLAEbAkoCv — Chandler Rome (@Chandler_Rome) October 16, 2026 MLB News Looking at how the Brewers swept the Dodgers to stamp their ticket to the World Series. A look at a fairly weak free agent class this offseason. Checking in on how the Rays managed to dig their way back in the ALCS. The Rays are heading home, one game away from heading to the World Series. How Drew Rasmussen helped carry his team to another essential win. Three storylines to watch in ALCS Game 6 tonight. Assessing Bo Bichette’s opt-in option for the coming season. The Rays figured out their winning formula just in the nick of time. What comes next for the Dodgers after being swept in the NLCS? Trea Turner is on notice to improve at shortstop or get moved. Notes from Arizona Fall League. ($) How Guardians fans lost out thanks to Mother Nature. ($) Comparing collapsing dynasties from the Yankees to the Dodgers. ($) This is very cool now, but who the heck would have spent $1000 on this back in 2014? Ah yes, those philanthropic billionaires. An old friend came to visit the Guardians. View this post on Instagram I’m not crying, you’re crying. View this post on Instagram

item.title: Kate Scott comes back to the Bay Area for historic WNBA Finals broadcast
item.description: Kate Scott of NBC Sports Philadelphia speaks before the game between the Philadelphia 76ers and the Atlanta Hawks at Xfinity Mobile Arena on Feb. 19, 2026 in Philadelphia. (Isaiah Vazquez/Getty Images) When Kate Scott was a student at UC Berkeley in the early 2000s, she was looking for any way to break into a sports broadcasting career. On Monday, two decades after she started her trailblazing career in the Bay Area, she's back in San Francisco to call a WNBA Finals game between the Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream. In her first year as USA Sports' top play-by-play broadcaster, her first-ever WNBA Finals game is back in the city that launched her career. "None of this feels real at all," Scott told SFGATE in a phone conversation on Saturday. "I often fall back on a quote from another Bay Area trailblazer Belva Davis - who I was lucky enough to meet at a luncheon years ago - when she was asked the same question, and it's the title of her book, which I have read cover-to-cover many times: This is never in my wildest dreams.'" Scott, 43, grew up in Central Valley in a sports-obsessed family and went to Clovis High School, where she caught the storytelling itch at her high school newspaper. As she arrived in Berkeley, she got on camera doing Cal football highlights and fell into broadcasting through calling high school football games. Kate Scott leads Cal students in cheers as the first female "mic man" in school history. (Photo courtesy of Kate Scott) Kate Scott poses with the other "mic men" who worked at Cal sporting events. (Photo courtesy of Kate Scott) Now, 21 years later, Scott will be the play-by-play broadcaster for Game 2 on Monday night and Game 3 on Wednesday night in Atlanta. She'll also call Games 5, 6 and 7, should the series between the Valkyries and the Dream go the distance. By doing so, Scott will be a part of more history in the sports broadcasting world. This year's WNBA Finals is the first time in the league's 30-year history where every television broadcaster in a multi-game series is a woman. USA's coverage will feature Sarah Kustok and Hall of Famer Tamika Catchings as analysts. Kustok is also the analyst for the other two games on NBC , with former women's basketball player Zora Stephenson handling play-by-play duties. The Valkyries are up 1-0 in the series after Saturday's come-from-behind victory . If the Dream win a single game and send this series past the minimum four games, Scott will be the first woman to be the play-by-play mic for a WNBA championship since Hannah Storm called the one-game inaugural title game in 1997. How would Scott approach calling the final moment for either the Dream or the Valkyries winning their first-ever title? "Your first thought as a broadcaster, or at least my first thought, is, ‘Don't f-k it up,'" Scott said with a laugh. "Because that is so special. And at the same time, what an incredible honor, what a phenomenal opportunity to get to be the voice of a moment that is going to l
item.content:encoded: Kate Scott of NBC Sports Philadelphia speaks before the game between the Philadelphia 76ers and the Atlanta Hawks at Xfinity Mobile Arena on Feb. 19, 2026 in Philadelphia. (Isaiah Vazquez/Getty Images) When Kate Scott was a student at UC Berkeley in the early 2000s, she was looking for any way to break into a sports broadcasting career. On Monday, two decades after she started her trailblazing career in the Bay Area, she's back in San Francisco to call a WNBA Finals game between the Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream. In her first year as USA Sports' top play-by-play broadcaster, her first-ever WNBA Finals game is back in the city that launched her career. "None of this feels real at all," Scott told SFGATE in a phone conversation on Saturday. "I often fall back on a quote from another Bay Area trailblazer Belva Davis - who I was lucky enough to meet at a luncheon years ago - when she was asked the same question, and it's the title of her book, which I have read cover-to-cover many times: This is never in my wildest dreams.'" Scott, 43, grew up in Central Valley in a sports-obsessed family and went to Clovis High School, where she caught the storytelling itch at her high school newspaper. As she arrived in Berkeley, she got on camera doing Cal football highlights and fell into broadcasting through calling high school football games. Kate Scott leads Cal students in cheers as the first female "mic man" in school history. (Photo courtesy of Kate Scott) Kate Scott poses with the other "mic men" who worked at Cal sporting events. (Photo courtesy of Kate Scott) Now, 21 years later, Scott will be the play-by-play broadcaster for Game 2 on Monday night and Game 3 on Wednesday night in Atlanta. She'll also call Games 5, 6 and 7, should the series between the Valkyries and the Dream go the distance. By doing so, Scott will be a part of more history in the sports broadcasting world. This year's WNBA Finals is the first time in the league's 30-year history where every television broadcaster in a multi-game series is a woman. USA's coverage will feature Sarah Kustok and Hall of Famer Tamika Catchings as analysts. Kustok is also the analyst for the other two games on NBC , with former women's basketball player Zora Stephenson handling play-by-play duties. The Valkyries are up 1-0 in the series after Saturday's come-from-behind victory . If the Dream win a single game and send this series past the minimum four games, Scott will be the first woman to be the play-by-play mic for a WNBA championship since Hannah Storm called the one-game inaugural title game in 1997. How would Scott approach calling the final moment for either the Dream or the Valkyries winning their first-ever title? "Your first thought as a broadcaster, or at least my first thought, is, ‘Don't f-k it up,'" Scott said with a laugh. "Because that is so special. And at the same time, what an incredible honor, what a phenomenal opportunity to get to be the voice of a moment that is going to live on forever in this sport." Networks sideline reporter Kate Scott broadcasts during the 120th Civil War NCAA football game between the Oregon Ducks and the Oregon State Beavers on Nov. 26, 2016, at Reser Stadium in Corvallis, Ore. (Brian Murphy/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Kate Scott on the microphone at KNBR 680 during her stint on the "Murph and Mac" morning show. (Photo courtesy of Kate Scott) Scott has been the "first woman" at many stops of her career , starting with being the first female "mic man" at Cal. Some standouts, among the others: she was the first woman to do play-by-play for an NFL game on the radio, announcing two 49ers preseason games in 2016, the first woman to call football games for the Pac-12 Network, the first woman to call a Golden State Warriors game as part of a special all-women broadcast in 2021, and the first woman to call an NFL regular-season game for national radio broadcaster Westwood One when she did a game in Dublin last year. Bay Area sports fans may remember Scott best for a five-year run on KNBR-AM/FM, when she joined the "Murph and Mac" morning show right during the heart of the Giants' 2010s dynasty. (She also did a year as a morning show host at rival station 95.7 The Game, joining the ever-growing list of Bay Area sports radio folks to work for both stations.) Scott said she's thought of those Giants teams as she's watched both WNBA Finals teams. "One of the reasons why the Giants' success in the last decade was so much fun was because so many saw ourselves in the undersized, pot-smoking Tim Lincecum. It was the same with the Warriors when they were at Oracle," Scott said. "There's just a communal joy that comes with that closeness. And the Valkyries have that in the Bay. They are such a great representative of every aspect of the Bay, whether it's Natalie Nakase and her Asian-American heritage or its Gabby Williams shouting out, ‘For the gays' on Pride Night. And it's the same in Atlanta when I'm there." Kate Scott interviews a player on the San Jose Giants, the Single-A affiliate of the San Francisco Giants. (Photo courtesy of Kate Scott) Kate Scott, center, smiles for a photo with longtime KNBR morning show hosts Paul McCaffrey (left) and Brian Murphy. Scott worked with the duo on the "Murph and Mac" show from 2011-2016. (Photo courtesy of Kate Scott) Scott is starting her sixth season as the play-by-play announcer for the NBA's Sixers this month, preparing for a season covering newly acquired stars LeBron James and Jaylen Brown. In the next two weeks, Scott will be jetting between SF, Atlanta and Philadelphia to do her play-by-play duties. "I'm very much expecting to have a wild next week-and-a-half," Scott said. Fortunately for her, the NBA's national TV interest in the new-look Sixers means Scott would only miss one Philly game if the WNBA Finals went to Game 7. (She said the Sixers already have a backup in place if it comes to that.) That game would have Scott back in San Francisco for a winner-take-all game on Halloween night. Scott, who met her wife, Nicole, in San Francisco, quipped she will "hop on Muni and go straight to the Castro and have a blast" after a possible seventh game. But no matter what happens in the series, Scott is just thrilled to have another moment of "kismet" in her already trailblazing career. Her first national television call of a championship was the NWSL title match - which was also hosted here in the Bay Area. But there's something extra for her about calling women's basketball, the sport Scott feels helped vault her career. Scott was a top play-by-play broadcaster at the Pac-12 Network in the 2010s, on the call when Sabrina Ionescu was a star at Oregon, Stanford was building the core of its 2021 national title-winning team and the Pac-12 was the best women's basketball conference in the country. "I'm not here calling LeBron James' final couple of seasons in the NBA without covering women's basketball in the Bay Area," Scott said. "I don't even know if I can find the words to explain just how special it is to be headed to the bay for my first call in these finals." Broadcaster Kate Scott and analyst Olympic gold medalist AJ Mleczko call the game between the Chicago Blackhawks and the St. Louis Blues at the United Center on March 8, 2020 in Chicago. (Chase Agnello-Dean/NHLI via Getty Images) She might not have the words for that moment, but she does have gratitude for the other women in the business who have helped her along the way. People like Mindi Bach, Tracey Watkowski, Jenn Violet Kennedy, Devon Fox, Mary Murphy and Krista Blunk helped Scott open doors to new career pathways and set her on the path to this point today. "People look at me and think I did this all on my own. I've had many male champions, but so many women helped me and played their ‘woman card' and said my name in the room when I was early in my career and still just trying to break in," Scott said as she began to tear up. "I

item.title: Enzo Maresca provides Erling Haaland injury update and confirms Antoine Semenyo blow
item.description: Enzo Maresca has provided an optimistic update on Erling Haaland ’s fitness but revealed that Antoine Semenyo will be sidelined for two months. Haaland was hurt in a challenge with Jack Clarke during Saturday’s win over Ipswich , during which the Norwegian bagged a brace, seeming to catch the Tractor Boys substitute after kicking the ball in injury time. Maresca stated after the match that he hoped Haaland’s issue was nothing serious and the striker will be assessed ahead of Tuesday’s Champions League clash with AEK Athens . "He can be available, we will see, we have a session now,” Maresca told a press conference. “We have some doubts after Sunday's game. He was quite good yesterday, better. So we will see today." Erling Haaland picked up an injury against Ipswich on the weekend (Reuters) With Haaland’s involvement up in the air, Maresca could be faced with the headache of replacing a player in the starting line-up who has scored 12 from 12 this season. "For sure, to replace Erling it is always difficult but we have some different options, we will see tomorrow,” he said. “It also depends on the game plan. There is also the chance that he can be available tomorrow. We'll see." Asked whether Phil Foden , who broke a 35-game run without scoring against Ipswich, could be an option up top, Maresca replied: " Yeah, Phil can be one of the solutions, not the only one. As you said, he already played in the past in that position so he can play now again. "But now, at the moment the number nine is Erling." City have meanwhile been dealt another blow to their attacking ranks with Maresca confirming that Semenyo will be out for “eight weeks”. The Ghanaian winger looked to be struggling with a leg problem after the final whistle against Ipswich but following his diagnosis, Maresca has taken solace from not having his worst fears realised, after initially being under the impression the injury was even more serious. "In the first moment we expected an even worse injury, so we were more worried, but after yesterday's scan we feel much better because it is not so big like we expected,” he said. "It could be eight weeks. So now in the moment, the most important thing for him is to recover and also when he is back, probably around December, we will have a new player in terms of energy. Antoine Semenyo is out for eight weeks with a leg injury (Getty) "It is a collateral [lower leg injury], something like this. It is not muscle, not a muscle problem." Maresca confirmed that the rest of his squad is “more or less OK”. On Semenyo and Haaland, Maresca added: "First of all to lose Antoine or any player for us, it is not good. Then in terms of Erling, we said that we can use Antoine as a nine but also we have different players that we are going to try and find new solutions. "We will see, again. At the moment it is Erling, why do we need to think about a different nine when Erling is there? Then, if something happens and we need a different plan or a different nine, we wi

Erling Haaland picked up an injury against Ipswich on the weekend (Reuters) With Haaland’s involvement up in the air, Maresca could be faced with the headache of replacing a player in the starting line-up who has scored 12 from 12 this season. "For sure, to replace Erling it is always difficult but we have some different options, we will see tomorrow,” he said. “It also depends on the game plan. There is also the chance that he can be available tomorrow. We'll see." Asked whether Phil Foden , who broke a 35-game run without scoring against Ipswich, could be an option up top, Maresca replied: " Yeah, Phil can be one of the solutions, not the only one. As you said, he already played in the past in that position so he can play now again. "But now, at the moment the number nine is Erling." City have meanwhile been dealt another blow to their attacking ranks with Maresca confirming that Semenyo will be out for “eight weeks”. The Ghanaian winger looked to be struggling with a leg problem after the final whistle against Ipswich but following his diagnosis, Maresca has taken solace from not having his worst fears realised, after initially being under the impression the injury was even more serious. "In the first moment we expected an even worse injury, so we were more worried, but after yesterday's scan we feel much better because it is not so big like we expected,” he said. "It could be eight weeks. So now in the moment, the most important thing for him is to recover and also when he is back, probably around December, we will have a new player in terms of energy. Antoine Semenyo is out for eight weeks with a leg injury (Getty) "It is a collateral [lower leg injury], something like this. It is not muscle, not a muscle problem." Maresca confirmed that the rest of his squad is “more or less OK”. On Semenyo and Haaland, Maresca added: "First of all to lose Antoine or any player for us, it is not good. Then in terms of Erling, we said that we can use Antoine as a nine but also we have different players that we are going to try and find new solutions. "We will see, again. At the moment it is Erling, why do we need to think about a different nine when Erling is there? Then, if something happens and we need a different plan or a different nine, we will see."

item.title: Bengals vs. Ravens odds: Opening lines for Week 7 may hint at Lamar Jackson’s status
item.description: The Cincinnati Bengals are coming off their bye week with a 3-2 record and are hopefully healthy, rested, and have all their kinks ironed out. They’re 0-1 in the AFC North, having lost to the Steelers in Week 3, but will get a chance to even their division record out in Week 7 when they travel to Baltimore to face the 4-2 Ravens. The Ravens are coming off a division loss of their own, dropping an ugly 13-10 loss to the Browns in Cleveland, but they’ve been without two-time NFL MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson, who suffered a rare medial sprain of his left ankle in Week 4. Jackson missed the entire week of practice before the Ravens’ Week 6 game and was ruled out prior to the game. It’s unclear as to whether or not he’ll be available against the Bengals, but his projected return is Week 7 or Week 8. As of right now, the Bengals are going into their Week 7 game as three-point underdogs in Baltimore, according to the FanDuel Sportsbook . This makes sense if Lamar plays, considering the ups and downs we’ve seen from both the Bengals’ offense and defense so far this season. But if Tyler Huntley were to start, the Bengals would likely be favored. If nothing else, the game would be closer to a pick ‘em, so it seems like the oddsmakers expect Lamar to suit up. Hopefully, the bye week gave Cincinnati time to figure things out. Stay tuned throughout the week for updates on both the Bengals and Ravens before their Week 7 matchup on Sunday in Baltimore. item.title: Real Madrid exchanging final paperwork with superstar’s agent after renewal agreement – Romano
item.description: Real Madrid exchanging final paperwork with superstar’s agent after renewal agreement – Romano Real Madrid have been busy of late, working to secure the futures of some of their most important players in the squad. Long-term renewal agreements have been reached with the midfield duo of Arda Guler and Jude Bellingham recently after Vinicius Jr.’s contract was extended during the summer. Beyond that, the Spanish capital heavyweights have also reached an agreement with Thibaut Courtois to extend his deal with the club for one more year until 2028. Documents being exchanged Building on that, Fabrizio Romano now states that documents are already being exchanged between Courtois’ lawyers and the Real Madrid camp, with only the final signature now being left. The Belgian veteran joined the Spanish giants from Chelsea in the summer of 2018 and has grown into one of the most important players in the team. During his time at the club, the 34-year-old shot-stopper has racked up 344 appearances in all competitions, keeping 131 clean sheets. In that time, he has won three La Liga titles and two UEFA Champions League trophies, along with several other titles. No signs of slowing down Despite having had to deal with some physical issues in the latter stages of his career, Courtois is still going very strong and remains one of the best goalkeepers in Europe. At 34 years old, the Belgian still has plenty left to offer at the highest level and he continues to showcase just that week in week out with the Merengues . Set to stay until 2028. (Photo by Tullio M. Puglia/Getty Images) Therefore, the one-year renewal from Real Madrid does not come as a surprise whatsoever, with a verbal agreement reached and documents now being exchanged. So far in the ongoing season, Courtois has played in all 11 games for Real Madrid this season, but has managed only two clean sheets, while letting in 13 goals. While the search for a long-term successor might already be taking place in the background, Real Madrid have moved to renew Courtois’ contract by one more season, with only the official signing on paper being left pending.

item.title: Browns Week 6 win in review: 4 downs lead us to shifting narratives
item.description: The Cleveland Browns are 4-2. Yes, you read that right. After trailing by double digits in the first half against a Baltimore Ravens team that was missing star quarterback Lamar Jackson, the Browns scored 13 unanswered points to improve to 4-2 on the season . It wasn’t pretty (in any way), but like before, the team found a way to win when it mattered the most . 1st Down: Another uneven offensive performance It’s going to be a persistent topic, but Cleveland’s offense struggled once again. Granted, the team wasn’t playing in a monsoon like last week, but the same issues that have been persistent all season were prevalent today. The run game has been nonexistent, and the passing game has been inconsistent, at best. Head coach Todd Monken didn’t do his offense any favors in the first half with his play-calling. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter pretty much bottled up the passing game by playing primarily zone, and the Baltimore defense did a great job dropping and getting to their spots. The Browns receivers struggled to get open, and Watson was hesitant to pull the trigger. Watson needs to just let it rip and be okay with making mistakes. Watson isn’t costing the team with his play, and he’s doing enough when they need him. Is it sustainable? No, but the consistency has to appear at some point. Overall, the offense was ineffective for most of the game but found a way to get something going late in the fourth quarter, again . 2nd Down: Let’s talk about the QB more In terms of the quarterback performance, Watson didn’t play well at all. However, when the team needed him, he found a way to get the job done. On paper, the stats are fine and not the worst. The film tells a different story. The flashes are brief, but his flaws are more noticeable. However, the team is finding a way to win despite that. Watson’s level of play isn’t necessarily sustainable, as I’ve mentioned before, but I do believe the Browns will be hesitant to pull the trigger on a quarterback change unless the team starts to lose. Everyone knows that the future quarterback isn’t on this team, but for years fans complained about not having competent quarterback play, which is what Watson is giving you. It’s not pretty, and it’s not flashy, but it’s better than what the team had previously, including from Watson. I am not saying that Watson has played well throughout the entire season, but he’s not playing at a level that screams “he needs to be benched.” Can the play be better? Yes. After trailing by double digits in the first half against a Baltimore Ravens team that was missing star quarterback Lamar Jackson, the Browns scored 13 unanswered points to improve to 4-2 on the season . Granted, the team wasn’t playing in a monsoon like last week, but the same issues that have been persistent all season were prevalent today. The run game has been nonexistent, and the passing game has been inconsistent, at best. Head coach Todd Monken didn’t do his offense any favors in the first half with his play-calling. The Browns receivers struggled to get open, and Watson was hesitant to pull the trigger. Watson needs to just let it rip and be okay with making mistakes. Watson isn’t costing the team with his play, and he’s doing enough when they need him. Is it sustainable? No, but the consistency has to appear at some point. Overall, the offense was ineffective for most of the game but found a way to get something going late in the fourth quarter, again . 2nd Down: Let’s talk about the QB more In terms of the quarterback performance, Watson didn’t play well at all. However, when the team needed him, he found a way to get the job done. On paper, the stats are fine and not the worst. The film tells a different story. The flashes are brief, but his flaws are more noticeable. However, the team is finding a way to win despite that. Watson’s level of play isn’t necessarily sustainable, as I’ve mentioned before, but I do believe the Browns will be hesitant to pull the trigger on a quarterback change unless the team starts to lose. Everyone knows that the future quarterback isn’t on this team, but for years fans complained about not having competent quarterback play, which is what Watson is giving you. It’s not pretty, and it’s not flashy, but it’s better than what the team had previously, including from Watson. I am not saying that Watson has played well throughout the entire season, but he’s not playing at a level that screams “he needs to be benched.” Can the play be better? Yes. But I don’t believe that the team needs to bench him right now and winning games will certainly keep him in place. 3rd Down: This defense might be really good How about this defense? Going into the offseason, I said that going from Jim Schwartz to Mike Rutenberg was going to be an upgrade. Six weeks in, the take seems to be aging well. Scheme-wise, it’s a major improvement from last season. One of the many complaints I had about Schwartz’s defense was how the scheme was predictable. Rutenberg’s scheme is anything but that. It’s more unpredictable, with much more chaos, and the players are thriving in it. Linebacker Carson Schwesinger had a fantastic game, and defensive tackle Maliek Collins continues to be a force in the interior. The Ravens running game was nonexistent today, and the passing defense did enough to contain wide receiver Zay Flowers. Granted, the Ravens didn’t have quarterback Lamar Jackson, but this was another strong performance by a legit defense. Is it better than last year’s? 4th Down- 4-2 is 4-2. The Cleveland Browns being 4-2 right now is a surprise, and we don’t have to lie to ourselves about it. The win wasn’t pretty, but the Browns are 4-2. With that being said, no one knows how good this Cleveland Browns team is right now. I don’t. You don’t. Are they a playoff team? As of now, they have the fourth seed, but on the field they are not playing playoff-level football. The offense still has issues, but the defense is playing at an elite level. It’s a question whether or not this team can find consistency on the offensive side of the ball or will the offense just stay at this level for the entire season. Being 4-2 is a lot better than being 1-5. Or 0-6. It’s a week-to-week league, and Cleveland is finding ways to win. Can’t complain about that. Extra points Wide receiver Jerry Jeudy is giving valid reasons why the Browns shouldn’t trade him. He’s well respected in the wide receiver room, and the team probably loses if he doesn’t have the game he had on Sunday Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion both struggled today, but it happens for young players. Jared Verse played well in the run game; need the pressures to convert to sacks soon. Might as well stop talking about the running game; it was already broken before the season, and it might be a while before it actually gets fixed. Whenever Cleveland sports teams play on the same day, it feels like a guarantee both teams will not win. Wish that had been different on Sunday. A day later, what are you thinking about the Browns, their Week 6 win, and the changing narratives around the team? Join the conversation! item.title: Oregon’s Evan Stewart arrested on DUI charge after sitting out Nebraska win
item.description: Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked into the Springfield Municipal Jail on a charge of driving under the influence of intoxicants early Sunday, hours after sitting out the Ducks’ comeback win over Nebraska with an undisclosed injury. A jail employee told KATU that Stewart was booked around 7 a.m. PT and released about an hour later to a third party whose name matches another Oregon wide receiver. Oregon hadn’t publicly responded to the report as of Monday morning. MORE: Big 12 admits mistake: Notre Dame deserved final play in controversial loss to BYU What happened with Evan Stewart? KATU sports reporter Hallie DeVore reported that Springfield police identified the third party as Dakorien Moore. Oregon’s sophomore receiver by that name is tied with Stewart for the team lead with four touchdown catches. Eugene station KVAL also confirmed the booking with the jail. KATU’s report followed social media posts claiming several Ducks players had been arrested over the weekend. Neither station has confirmed any other arrests, and no details on the circumstances behind Stewart’s charge have been released. MORE: When was Miami last ranked No. 1? Hurricanes could end long wait in new AP Top 25 Oregon’s top receiver already sidelined Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart runs with the ball against the UCLA Bruins | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Stewart opened last week as questionable on Oregon’s availability report, dropped to doubtful Thursday and was ruled out with an undisclosed injury before Saturday’s 11 p.m. ET kickoff. He leads the Ducks with 27 catches for 352 yards, and his 44-yard touchdown in the 17-15 home loss to UCLA on Oct. 10 pulled Oregon within two points. The Ducks were also without quarterback Dante Moore, who’s missed two straight games with a concussion suffered against USC, and receiver Jeremiah McClellan. Oregon coach Dan Lanning replaced starter Brock Thomas with Dylan Raiola in the fourth quarter, and the former Nebraska quarterback beat his old team with a 4-yard touchdown pass to tight end Jamari Johnson with 28 seconds left. Lanning pointed to the missing pieces after the 17-14 win. “That being said, it does look like a different group than what we started the season with ,” Lanning said. “You thought you’re going to have Jeremiah McClellan, Evan Stewart, right? item.title: Stan Van Gundy Doubts New-Look Timberwolves—and He Might Be Right
item.description: NBA on Prime analyst Stan Van Gundy at press conference at T-Mobile Arena. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Daniel Benjamin, Editor The Minnesota Timberwolves upgraded their roster because reaching the Western Conference semifinals was not enough. They brought in LaMelo Ball to give Anthony Edwards a new playmaking partner. However, the team also decided to move on from two proven frontcourt scorers. This major change creates a risky balance, and that balance is the main reason why Stan Van Gundy is skeptical about the move. The trade fixed Minnesota’s backcourt problems but created new questions in the Wolves frontcourt . Van Gundy wonders if the team lost too much scoring power near the basket just to get a better passing guard. Ball gives Edwards better shot quality, but losing two big men hurts defense and rebounding. Championship teams need both inside and outside strength. Stan Van Gundy Questions Timberwolves’ Upgrade Van Gundy shared his assessment on The Zach Lowe Show . Van Gundy doubts Minnesota improved, though he expects the team to finish in the West’s top six, saying, “Most people are saying Minnesota is better, I just don’t see that at all…I think they’re a pretty solid sixth (seed) in my opinion.” Stan Van Gundy on the addition of LaMelo Ball to the Timberwolves: “Most people are saying Minnesota is better, I just don’t see that at all…I think they’re a pretty solid sixth (seed) in my opinion” (via @ZachLowe_NBA) https://t.co/UU560QGArS — Kyle Ingram (@SnapshotKyle) October 18, 2026 Van Gundy thinks the new backcourt will score and entertain, though scoring alone will not lift Minnesota. He places Oklahoma City, San Antonio, Denver, and Houston above the Timberwolves, though Minnesota might still catch the Lakers. LaMelo Ball Could Take Pressure Off Anthony Edwards Minnesota Timberwolves guard LaMelo Ball (1) drives past Indiana Pacers forward Obi Toppin (1) at James H. Hilton Coliseum. Photo Credit: Reese Strickland, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect Minnesota targeted Ball to fix a clear roster need. item.content:encoded: NBA on Prime analyst Stan Van Gundy at press conference at T-Mobile Arena. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Daniel Benjamin, Editor The Minnesota Timberwolves upgraded their roster because reaching the Western Conference semifinals was not enough. They brought in LaMelo Ball to give Anthony Edwards a new playmaking partner. However, the team also decided to move on from two proven frontcourt scorers. This major change creates a risky balance, and that balance is the main reason why Stan Van Gundy is skeptical about the move. The trade fixed Minnesota’s backcourt problems but created new questions in the Wolves frontcourt . Van Gundy wonders if the team lost too much scoring power near the basket just to get a better passing guard. Ball gives Edwards better shot quality, but losing two big men hurts defense and rebounding. Championship teams need both inside and outside strength. Stan Van Gundy Questions Timberwolves’ Upgrade Van Gundy shared his assessment on The Zach Lowe Show . Van Gundy doubts Minnesota improved, though he expects the team to finish in the West’s top six, saying, “Most people are saying Minnesota is better, I just don’t see that at all…I think they’re a pretty solid sixth (seed) in my opinion.” Stan Van Gundy on the addition of LaMelo Ball to the Timberwolves: “Most people are saying Minnesota is better, I just don’t see that at all…I think they’re a pretty solid sixth (seed) in my opinion” (via @ZachLowe_NBA) https://t.co/UU560QGArS — Kyle Ingram (@SnapshotKyle) October 18, 2026 Van Gundy thinks the new backcourt will score and entertain, though scoring alone will not lift Minnesota. He places Oklahoma City, San Antonio, Denver, and Houston above the Timberwolves, though Minnesota might still catch the Lakers. LaMelo Ball Could Take Pressure Off Anthony Edwards Minnesota Timberwolves guard LaMelo Ball (1) drives past Indiana Pacers forward Obi Toppin (1) at James H. Hilton Coliseum. Photo Credit: Reese Strickland, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect Minnesota targeted Ball to fix a clear roster need. While Edwards averaged 28.8 points last season, he often had to manufacture his own shots when the offense stalled. Ball adds a second playmaker who can jump-start the transition game, spot-cut teammates, and generate easy scoring opportunities before opposing defenses can set up. Ball averaged 20.1 points, 4.8 rebounds and 7.1 assists in 72 games for Charlotte last season, shooting 36.8% from three. Those numbers do not guarantee a clean fit, but they show his potential value. Edwards can keep scoring while attacking after defenses have already reacted to Ball. That is the idea behind giving Minnesota another answer when playoff defenses take away its first option . For the upgrade to hold, Ball must also stay healthy and limit rushed decisions that turn his aggressive passing into empty possessions. The connection may also help Rudy Gobert around the basket. If Ball uses screens patiently and delivers the ball on time, Gobert should get more chances near the rim. Minnesota needed a different kind of creator, not another player expected to imitate Edwards. Losing Julius Randle and Naz Reid Is the Cost Van Gundy’s doubt becomes clearer when the outgoing production is taken into account. Julius Randle averaged 21.1 points, 6.7 rebounds and 5.0 assists last season. Naz Reid added 13.6 points and 6.2 rebounds. Together, they supplied 34.7 points and 12.9 rebounds per game. Randle handled the ball and scored against mismatches. Reid provided bench scoring and floor spacing, while covering center minutes when Gobert rested. Replacing that production is not as simple as redistributing shots. Jonathan Kuminga adds athleticism and scoring potential, but Minnesota must still prove it has enough frontcourt size, rebounding and reliable offense. Ball improves one part of the roster, but he cannot automatically solve the problems created by those departures. Sixth Place Is Plausible, Not Inevitable Minnesota finished 49-33 and sixth in the West last season. The Wolves defeated Denver in the first round, then lost to San Antonio in the semifinals. Van Gundy’s projection is not unreasonable. The conference is strong, and Minnesota has questions about fit, depth and defense. Still, sixth place is a forecast, not proof that the trade failed. Minnesota’s case for becoming a dark-horse contender with Ball rests on whether he and Edwards make each other more effective while the supporting cast replaces enough of the lost production. The test is whether the new offense works in difficult games, not whether Ball’s arrival looks exciting in October. The Last Word Van Gundy correctly questions the Timberwolves frontcourt because losing the productive Reid and Randle will have consequences. However, Ball gives Edwards another creator and provides Gobert with a potential pick-and-roll partner. The Timberwolves ultimately traded frontcourt security for more backcourt playmaking, meaning the success of this gamble depends entirely on Ball’s and Kuminga’s fit along with their unproven supporting cast. More NBA News Timberwolves’ Reserves Make Final Cases For Rotation In Loss vs Bulls Timberwolves Are Taking A Risk With Their Center Depth This Season LaMelo Ball Gives Timberwolves New Way to Use Rudy Gobert Photo Credit: Kirby Lee, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect

item.title: ‘It’s very simple’ – Luis Enrique talks trying to stop Lamine Yamal and Barcelona
item.description: BARCELONA, SPAIN - OCTOBER 1: (L-R)Paris Saint Germain coach Luis Enrique, Lamine Yamal of FC Barcelona, Ibrahim Mbaye of Paris Saint Germain, Nuno Mendes of Paris Saint Germain during the UEFA Champions League match between FC Barcelona v Paris Saint Germain at the Lluis Companys Olympic Stadium on October 1, 2025 in Barcelona Spain (Photo by David Ramirez/Soccrates/Getty Images) | Getty Images Paris Saint-Germain boss Luis Enrique was quizzed on how to stop Lamine Yamal ahead of Tuesday’s Champions League clash with Barcelona. Yamal heads into the match in stunning form and after scoring a brilliant goal during Barcelona’s win over Real Betis at the weekend. Lucho says the best way to defend against Yamal is to make sure he doesn’t get on the ball. “It’s very simple. The best way to defend against Lamine Yamal is to have the ball. That’s our ideal, but it won’t be like that because we know how difficult it is to play against Barça,” he told a news conference. “We must concentrate on what we can do. We know they have many high-quality players; Lamine isn’t the only one. Raphinha, Pedri, Cubarsí, Joan Garcia… there are many. We will stay focused and alert. We must overcome this as a team. “We know Barcelona, ​​I love watching their games, I adore their style of play. It will be difficult because of their quality players; small details can make the difference. There are very good individual players on both teams, but the victory has to be a collective one. They have a great sense of belonging. I know it will be a great match. “ Luis Enrique also says that both he and his team are relishing the thought of becoming the first team to beat Hansi Flick’s side in 2026-27. “It’s a motivation for us,” he added. “We’re motivated to be the only team to beat Barça this season. “I’m very connected to Barça, but I’m the coach of PSG. At first, I found it difficult to play against Barça, but I got used to it. They have very high-quality players, a sporting team with strong values. Nevertheless, I want to win tomorrow; it’s a major motivation to face the club that has meant the most to me in my career. “Hansi Flick has improved the results and instilled a style of play similar to the one he had at Bayern. We’ll have to attack if we want to win. We’re motivated to take the ball away from them. It’s a big challenge for us. We’ll see what happens tomorrow.” While Barca have been perfect this season, PSG have won both Champions League games but have won only four of seven Ligue 1 outings so far this season.

item.title: Medical Update | Francisco Conceicao
item.description: Medical Update | Francisco Conceicao Following the injury to his left shoulder sustained during the match against Lazio, Francisco Conceicao underwent diagnostic tests this morning at J|medical. The tests revealed a glenohumeral dislocation, which had already been reduced yesterday evening. The player will undergo conservative treatment and has already begun a rehabilitation programme aimed at a return to competitive action.

item.title: Arsenal and Spurs keeping tabs on La Liga starlet
item.description: Arsenal and Spurs keeping tabs on La Liga starlet Arsenal and Tottenham track Xavi Espart as Barcelona set demanding transfer terms Xavi Espart has attracted attention from both sides of north London, but Barcelona have already put substantial protection around his future. Arsenal and Tottenham are reportedly scouting the 19-year-old defender, whose new contract includes a release clause exceeding €100 million. The interest reflects the appeal of a young full-back comfortable in possession and capable of operating in several positions. The difficulty for any prospective buyer lies in persuading Barcelona to discuss a departure so soon after securing his long-term commitment. According to CaughtOffside , both Premier League clubs have watched Espart in person and prepared detailed reports. Their interest has not progressed to formal negotiations, leaving this as a developing scouting story rather than an imminent transfer. IMAGO Xavi Espart attracts north London scouting attention CaughtOffside’s report, citing sources close to the agents industry, places Arsenal and Tottenham among several clubs following Espart’s progress. Aston Villa, Borussia Dortmund and Juventus are also monitoring the La Masia graduate. That range of reported interest suggests his performances are drawing attention beyond Spain, although it does not establish that any club is preparing an offer. Espart’s technical quality, positional understanding and versatility are the attributes highlighted in the report. For clubs assessing young defenders, that combination offers potential value across different roles and systems. The challenge is judging how those qualities will develop with greater experience. At 19, Espart is being assessed both for what he can contribute now and for the player he might become. Watching him live and compiling reports are part of that process. They give interested clubs a basis for future decisions without committing them to a pursuit. Barcelona contract creates significant transfer obstacle Barcelona awarded Espart a professional contract running until June 2030 on July 1, 2026. The agreement includes a release clause worth more than €100 million. That clause should be distinguished from a negotiated asking price. It does not establish that a buying club would necessarily have to pay the full amount, but it reinforces Barcelona’s control over any potential departure. CaughtOffside places Espart’s current market value at around €25 million. It also reports that Barcelona would require an offer in the region of €40 million to €50 million, plus bonuses, before considering discussions. Those figures describe different things: an estimated valuation, a reported threshold for talks and a contractual release clause. None amounts to an agreed transfer fee. With several years remaining on the deal, Barcelona face no immediate contractual pressure to sell. Arsenal, Tottenham or another interested club would therefore need to make a compelling proposal simply
item.content:encoded: Arsenal and Spurs keeping tabs on La Liga starlet Arsenal and Tottenham track Xavi Espart as Barcelona set demanding transfer terms Xavi Espart has attracted attention from both sides of north London, but Barcelona have already put substantial protection around his future. Arsenal and Tottenham are reportedly scouting the 19-year-old defender, whose new contract includes a release clause exceeding €100 million. The interest reflects the appeal of a young full-back comfortable in possession and capable of operating in several positions. The difficulty for any prospective buyer lies in persuading Barcelona to discuss a departure so soon after securing his long-term commitment. According to CaughtOffside , both Premier League clubs have watched Espart in person and prepared detailed reports. Their interest has not progressed to formal negotiations, leaving this as a developing scouting story rather than an imminent transfer. IMAGO Xavi Espart attracts north London scouting attention CaughtOffside’s report, citing sources close to the agents industry, places Arsenal and Tottenham among several clubs following Espart’s progress. Aston Villa, Borussia Dortmund and Juventus are also monitoring the La Masia graduate. That range of reported interest suggests his performances are drawing attention beyond Spain, although it does not establish that any club is preparing an offer. Espart’s technical quality, positional understanding and versatility are the attributes highlighted in the report. For clubs assessing young defenders, that combination offers potential value across different roles and systems. The challenge is judging how those qualities will develop with greater experience. At 19, Espart is being assessed both for what he can contribute now and for the player he might become. Watching him live and compiling reports are part of that process. They give interested clubs a basis for future decisions without committing them to a pursuit. Barcelona contract creates significant transfer obstacle Barcelona awarded Espart a professional contract running until June 2030 on July 1, 2026. The agreement includes a release clause worth more than €100 million. That clause should be distinguished from a negotiated asking price. It does not establish that a buying club would necessarily have to pay the full amount, but it reinforces Barcelona’s control over any potential departure. CaughtOffside places Espart’s current market value at around €25 million. It also reports that Barcelona would require an offer in the region of €40 million to €50 million, plus bonuses, before considering discussions. Those figures describe different things: an estimated valuation, a reported threshold for talks and a contractual release clause. None amounts to an agreed transfer fee. With several years remaining on the deal, Barcelona face no immediate contractual pressure to sell. Arsenal, Tottenham or another interested club would therefore need to make a compelling proposal simply to open a conversation. Hansi Flick comparison highlights Espart’s qualities Hansi Flick has offered a striking assessment of the teenager, drawing a comparison with Philipp Lahm. “When I watch Xavi Espart play, I like his confidence on the ball. He reminds me of Philipp Lahm,” Flick said, in comments reported by Football España. The emphasis on confidence in possession helps explain the attention around Espart. It also provides a more specific insight than the broader excitement that often accompanies an emerging academy player. For Arsenal, his reported ability to operate in different positions could appeal to Mikel Arteta’s preference for defenders comfortable moving into midfield. Tottenham could regard him as a longer-term option, particularly amid reported interest in Pedro Porro from Barcelona and Real Madrid. However, no agreement involving Porro or connection between the two players’ futures has been established. January move remains distant prospect For now, the clearest distinction is between interest and action. Arsenal and Tottenham are watching Espart, while Barcelona have a lengthy contract and demanding reported financial expectations. A January transfer would require substantial progress from that starting point. There is currently no reported formal negotiation to suggest such a move is gathering pace. Espart’s continued development will determine whether the scouting attention becomes something more concrete. Further evidence of his quality could strengthen interest, but it could also reinforce Barcelona’s desire to keep him. The immediate story is therefore one of competing assessments: interested clubs see a promising defender worth following, while Barcelona’s contract arrangements underline how firmly they intend to control his future.

item.title: Bayern and Luis Díaz warm up for Arsenal revenge mission with furious rout of Leipzig | Andy Brassell
item.description: Bruised Bundesliga champions hit a supposed rival for six and their flying winger is peaking at a perfect moment When Bayern Munich fail to win for two games in a row, you know what is coming next. Particularly on a Saturday night showcase, against the sort of good domestic opposition that tend to bring the best out of the champions. It had been a frustrating week, domestically and continentally, in two games on the road. On both occasions they had been caught cold, conceding the Bundesliga’s fastest goal at Augsburg and going 1-0 down in less than 90 seconds in Stavanger . Vincent Kompany’s low profile on the Allianz Arena touchline, sat almost motionless in his seat on the bench as his team rattled a flurry of goals past poor RB Leipzig, had nothing to do with any lingering chagrin connected to those slow starts from his team. The sporting director, Max Eberl, who stood in for his coach in the post-match press conference, explained that the Belgian had been ill, not to mention Kompany’s current hip problem that had made the move from dressing room to pitch side slow and uncomfortable. Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: pressure mounts on Slegers as Hemp closes on record
item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. In contrast, Birmingham scored with their one shot on target as Océane Hurtré took her impressive tally to six in six. Sophie Downey Match report: Arsenal 1-1 Birmingham Continue reading...

Her deal was due to expire after next summer’s World Cup and this gives her the chance to lead the Lionesses to three European championship titles in a row. Wiegman, who took on the role in September 2021 , also led her native Netherlands to Euros glory in 2017 and has reached the final of the past five major tournaments, twice finishing as a World Cup runner-up. item.title: At Strasbourg, Gio Reyna is starting to gain what had been elusive: momentum
item.description: A goal against PSG is proof on the scoresheet of what can be seen on the teamsheet: At long last, Reyna is getting consistent minutes. For an entire four-year cycle, to write about Gio Reyna was to write about his potential – especially the nagging feeling that it was going unfulfilled. Once hyped as possibly the greatest prospect in US men’s history, a series of injuries kept him from simply taking the field, much less making his mark on it. Since his emergent 2020-21 season, when he logged nearly 2,000 Bundesliga minutes running alongside Erling Haaland, Jude Bellingham, and Jadon Sancho, Reyna finished each of the ensuing five seasons without even cresting 630 league minutes. “Rotational” became a generous descriptor for his role at Nottingham Forest on loan, and then last season with Borussia Mönchengladbach. Still, Gregg Berhalter and Mauricio Pochettino kept involving Reyna with the US squad based on that pesky potential – betting that, on his day, he still had the raw talent to do what few compatriots could. Continue reading...

item.description: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of the Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun. Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble.
